#2095. Serie B, si chiude la 13ª giornata: Pisa-Modena, big match. Sampdoria a Padova

Dopo la scorpacciata di gol di ieri sera, quando è andata in scena la prima metà del turno infrasettimanale, con ben 24 reti segnate in sei gare il campionato di Serie B anche oggi promette tanto spettacolo con sfide molto interessanti. Ad aprire le danze, alle 19:00, sarà una Cremonese in salute, ma desiderosa di rifarsi dal ko contro il SudTirol, che affronterà un Avellino che non vuole abdicare ai sogni di play off. A seguire ci sarà il big match di giornata che vedrà contrapposte all'Arena Garibaldi il Pisa e il Modena, due candidate alla promozione diretta: gli emiliani sono secondi e devono rispondere presente al Palermo, mentre i nerazzurri vogliono proseguire nella scalata verso le prime due piazze dopo un andamento finora altalenante. Il Mantova invece sarà chiamato a invertire la rotta, dopo quattro gare senza successi, sfidando un Arezzo che finora ha fatto meglio in trasferta che in casa. Infine la Sampdoria che cercherà di mettere in fila il quarto successo di fila, e magari allontanare definitivamente l'incubo retrocessione, sfidando un Padova che ha pareggiato le ultime tre.

#2093. Update on Watford’s pursuit of Edward Iordanescu as new boss talks stall

Watford swiftly turned their attention to Edward Iordanescu after parting ways with Alessio Dionisi on Sunday. The Hornets sacked the Italian following a 4-0 defeat against Sheffield United.

Yesterday, it was reported that Iordanescu had verbally agreed to become the new head coach at Vicarage Road, with the hope that he could take charge of Wednesday’s fixture against Blackburn Rovers. However, a new update from Sky Sports’ Anthony Joseph states that the Romanian is still in talks over his contract length and has not travelled to England yet.

The club remain hopeful of sealing the deal despite the setback. Iordanescu has been out of management since October 2025, when he departed Legia Warsaw.

He has mostly managed in his homeland, alongside spells in Poland and Bulgaria. A move to England would be the first in his career, should it be completed.

Watford have lost three of their last six matches, with their last defeat against Sheffield United. Although their defensive vulnerabilities stood out against the Blades, their attacking weaknesses have been more evident this season.

Clubs including Burnley, Bolton and Cardiff City have conceded more than Watford this season, while 16 teams have conceded less.

The Hornets are currently the lowest scorers in the Championship with 13 goals. Amin Nabizada is the club’s leading scorer with three goals, ahead of Myron Boadu on two. Furthermore, Watford have failed to score in seven matches so far this season. They also rank 19th in shots per match this season, highlighting the lack of creativity in the side.

As a coach, Iordanescu’s philosophies place an emphasis on defensive organisation. This could help Watford, but they need to improve in the attacking department more.

The Romanian manager, should he join Watford, would bring international pedigree and trophies from his homeland.

However, Iordanescu has been at nine clubs in fifteen years, so he isn’t exactly a boss to build a long-term dynasty. He is yet to manage in England as well, which marks a risk in a likely Championship relegation fight.

Burnley opted for Fabio Celestini in their managerial search, another boss without English experience, and he is yet to turn his side’s form around.

Iordanescu would have the January transfer window around the corner to shape the squad to his liking. His impact will need to be immediate, as concerns grow at Vicarage Road.

#2092. Attacco Inter, solo Pio sta bene. Chivu potrebbe essere costretto a fare questa mossa

Attacco Inter, solo Pio sta bene. Chivu potrebbe essere costretto a fare questa mossa

Cristian Chivu deve fare i conti con un attacco spuntato. In vista della gara contro lo Stoccarda, il tecnico può contare su tre attaccanti, ma solo Pio Esposito è in forma. Infatti, Thuram non è al meglio e Lautaro è tornato domenica dopo un infortunio che lo ha tenuto in infermeria più di un mese. A proposito del capitano nerazzurro, la Gazzetta dello Sport sottolinea come il rientro contro l'Atalanta non ha lasciato una buona impressione.

"L’infortunio muscolare a una coscia lo ha tenuto fuori per un mese, dicono che al momento abbia nelle gambe 30-40 minuti. Cristian Chivu potrebbe essere costretto a utilizzarlo lo stesso dal primo minuto perché Marcus Thuram ha accusato un affaticamento".

"Nel caso, il francese subentrerebbe al capitano in corso d’opera. Bonny, la quarta punta, è fermo da giorni. L’Inter si ritrova con un attacco massacrato dagli acciacchi. Pio Esposito è l’unico che sta bene. Avrebbe bisogno di rifiatare, ma non è possibile risparmiargli nulla. In fondo ha 21 anni, età in cui le capacità di recupero sono elevate. Thuram e Pio Esposito hanno condiviso 51 partite - non sempre per intero - e nei loro periodi assieme hanno segnato molto: 34 gol in due, 20 il francese e 14 l’azzurro. La coppia è assortita all’insegna della fisicità, la possanza di Pio si incastra con la corsa di Thuram. Un duo perfetto per assaltare lo Stoccarda, ma soltanto alle 20 sapremo quale sarà l’attacco. Non si può escludere niente".

#2091. Montella: "La Roma può lottare fino in fondo per lo scudetto. Il Milan di Amorim mi piace"

Nel corso della sua intervista per l'edizione odierna della Gazzetta dello Sport, Vincenzo Montella ha parlato del Milan: "Il gioco di Amorim mi ha convinto, va lasciato libero di imporre le sue idee. Mi piace anche Gonçalo Ramos ma bisogna dargli tempo. Non è che se ti hanno pagato 70 milioni allora automaticamente fai venti gol nella prima metà di stagione. Ci vogliono tempo e fiducia: può fare bene sia da unica punta che con un altro attaccante".

Da ex attaccante giallorosso, ha poi parlato della Roma e di Malen che a Parma ha realizzato quattro reti eguagliando il record di Montella in un derby: "Per me ne può fare anche cinque, è fortissimo e la Roma gioca bene e si diverte. Certo, io li avevo fatti in un derby, marcato da Nesta. Hanno un peso un po’ diverso. A parte questo, penso che l’olandese sarà il capocannoniere del campionato. Se continua così può fare trenta o più gol".

Infine un tema che a Roma è considerato ancora molto delicato, ovvero quello dello scudetto. L'ultima volta, con l'Aeroplanino in campo, fu 25 anni fa e adesso la squadra di Gasperini occupa le prime posizioni: "Possono lottare fino in fondo. Devono stare lì fino alla fine e poi chissà".

#2090. Inter, cessione in arrivo? Si può chiudere addirittura a giorni perché...

Inter, cessione in arrivo? Si può chiudere addirittura a giorni perché...

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui

In casa Inter si lavora a 360° anche sul mercato. In cassa potrebbe presto arrivare un margine non banale da eventualmente reinvestire già entro gennaio sui fronti individuati dalla società. L'aggiornamento arriva direttamente dall'argentina, proposto da Diario Olé.

Perché quella di sabato potrebbe essere l'ultima partita di Thomas Palacios con la maglia dell'Estudiantes. Il futuro del difensore argentino tiene banco a pochi giorni dalla finale di Copa Libertadores per un motivo ben chiaro: l'irruzione del River Plate. I Milionarios secondo i media argentini sono addirittura in trattativa avanzata con l'Inter, ma la partita non è ancora chiusa. Prevalentemente per un motivo, sottolineato anche da Diario Olé: l'Estudiantes potrebbe esercitare a stretto giro il diritto di riscatto fissato a 6,5 milioni di euro.

A quel punto si aprirebbero due scenari: quello più scontato porterebbe alla permanenza del ragazzo, ma non è da sottovalutare anche l'ipotesi che il riscatto dall'Inter sia poi il primo passo per rivendere Palacios a una cifra più alta a un altro club. In ogni caso Palacios non sarà titolare contro il Palmeiras perché ha un problema ai menischi. In futuro prossimo potrebbe persino sottoporsi a un intervento chirurgico. Per il momento ha evitato l'operazione proprio per non compromettere la partecipazione a questa finale. Al momento il difensore centrale mancino è in prestito all'Estudiantes fino alla fine del 2026. Il suo cartellino appartiene all'Inter, che rimane in attesa di segnali dall'Estudiantes e intanto dialoga con il River Plate.

#2088. Di Canio esalta il Napoli e Allegri: “Meritavano di più”, poi che parole per un azzurro

Nessuno se lo aspettava e invece il Napoli è stato protagonista di una grandissima prestazione all’Etihad contro il Manchester City. Gli azzurri non solo hanno tenuto una grande gara dal punto di vista difensivo, ma anche in attacco e in molti hanno elogiato la lettura del match di Allegri che è riuscito a imbrigliare Maresca e i Citizens.

Bella prova di diversi calciatori, Beukema è apparso tornato ai suoi livelli e dietro con Rrahmani ha offerto una grandissima prestazione. A centrocampo Gilmour ha regalato l’assist per il gol a Hojlund e ha disputato una gara di altissima intensità. Nonostante qualche critica sull’identità della squadra, Di Canio stavolta ha applaudito gli azzurri e la lettura di Allegri.

Da un lato belle parole per il Napoli e Allegri, dall’altro qualche velata critica al Manchester City e a Maresca che, da qualche settimana, vivono un momento piuttosto difficile. Intervenuto ai microfoni di SKY Sport, l’ex calciatore e ora commentatore televisivo Paolo Di Canio è stato piuttosto netto su questa sfida:

“Ho visto un Gilmour monumentale in mezzo al campo, complimenti anche ad Allegri per come ha letto la partita. Maresca invece non ha capito molto tatticamente, devo dire che il Napoli meritava di più”, la chiusura di Di Canio.

#2087. Key midfielder set for assessment as latest Blackburn Rovers injury update emerges for Watford test

Blackburn Rovers’ key midfielder Sam Morsy was absent from their 2-2 draw with Burnley after sustaining a knock in training. However, he is aiming to return to Championship action on Wednesday night against a managerless Watford.

The experienced Egyptian has been an ever-present in Rovers’ side this term since signing in the summer. Morsy has featured on 14 occasions in the league, but is facing a race to be fit in time. On his fitness, caretaker boss Damien Johnson told the Lancashire Telegraph: “Sam was touch and go for the weekend and is similar. He is still being assessed this morning. We will have more news on that after training.”

Meanwhile, Tom Atcheson is under concussion protocols after coming off early against Burnley, following a hit to the head. The academy graduate has also been a regular feature with his impressive performances at the heart of defence seeing him keep his place in the Northern Ireland national team.

Blackburn Rovers have been spearheaded by the sensational form of Andri Gudjohnsen, who is only behind Will Lankshear in the goalscoring charts with 11 to his name. But, it has been a collective effort to see them sit in 13th place.

Rovers were showing signs of real promise prior to Tony Mowbray stepping away from the dugout, most notably an impressive 2-1 victory over West Ham before the international break, with Morsy and Atcheson firmly part of that.

Morsy has filled the role as the anchor of Rovers’ midfield admirably and has shown his worth as one of the Championship’s finest midfield operators at 35.

Atcheson meanwhile is at the opposite end of his career, but has been just as influential. He usually plays on the right-hand side of the back three and impresses with his desire to orchestrate attacks from deep.

Both Morsy and Atcheson are vital cogs in Blackburn’s machine and they will be desperate to have the pair available for a favourable-looking encounter against a troubled Watford side.

Hoping to close the gap to the play-off places to just two points with a victory, Blackburn will certainly fancy their chances with the opponents registering a solitary victory in their last five outings.

Morsy’s experience has been vital for midfield partner Kristi Montgomery who is enjoying his breakout campaign at Ewood Park, and his quality on the ball is still there for all to see at 36.

Nonetheless, Moussa Baradji stepped up to fill his shoes last time out, while Gady Beyuku also strengthened his case for a starting berth in place of Atcheson so Johnson has a wealth of options should either of his key players be unavailable.

#2086. Romario chiede a Guardiola di diventare ct del Brasile. E lui: "Le caipirinha sono ottime..."

Ancora libero da contratti l'ex tecnico del Manchester City e del Barcellona, Pep Guardiola, è stato ospite del podcast di Romario. La leggenda brasiliana, che solo qualche giorno fa ha invitato il commissario tecnico verdeoro Carlo Ancelotti a "fare le valige", ha chiesto a Pep se un giorno vorrebbe allenare il Brasile.

Guardiola ha risposto con una battuta: "Le caipirinha sono ottime…". E Romario lo ha incalzato: “In Brasile abbiamo tante altre cose belle!”. Guardiola ha chiosato: “Allora ne parleremo più tardi”.

Nel corso della chiacchierata, Guardiola ha anche parlato del caso Cristiano Ronaldo: “La Federazione portoghese di calcio deve garantire a Cristiano Ronaldo una conclusione dignitosa della carriera, ha detto. "Entrambe le parti devono fare uno sforzo per garantire un addio all'altezza. Cristiano Ronaldo non dovrebbe lasciare la nazionale portoghese in questo modo. Non possono lasciarlo andare così", ha spiegato.

Poi ha aggiunto: "È stato una figura incredibilmente importante, non solo per sé stesso e per il Portogallo, ma anche per le future generazioni di calciatori portoghesi. Devono capire che Cristiano Ronaldo merita di andarsene alle sue condizioni. Ci sono giocatori eccezionali, e Cristiano Ronaldo è uno di loro; quindi questa situazione va risolta. Che la risolvano o no non mi riguarda, ma devono assolutamente farlo. È proprio così; ciò che ha realizzato nel mondo del calcio merita una conclusione diversa. Dovrebbe esserci una celebrazione in cui senta l'affetto dei suoi connazionali e, a sua volta, anche lui deve prendere l'iniziativa e dire: Voltiamo pagina sul passato. Non si dovrebbe giudicare un'intera carriera in base a un mese o due, o a causa di un disaccordo o di un malinteso con una o due persone. Ci sono carriere piene di successi che meritano di essere preservate e difese. I grandi giocatori, quelli che sono stati davvero al vertice del loro gioco, meritano di andarsene a testa alta. In primo luogo, perché se lo sono guadagnato con tutto ciò che hanno dato allo sport; è lo stesso calcio a dovere loro questo riconoscimento. E in secondo luogo, per i bambini che fanno i primi passi in campo, che potrebbero dire: Voglio concludere la mia carriera come Romário, Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi, Paolo Maldini o uno degli altri grandi della storia".

#2083. EFL club hit with unprecedented FA punishment – it's never happened before

Millwall have been handed a partial-stadium closure for their upcoming clash with Sheffield United in the EFL Championship, with the FA handing them an unprecedented punishment after ableist and homophobic chanting during their game with Charlton Athletic.

The chanting took place in the clash between Millwall and Charlton at the Den in January 2026 - a game that finished 4-0 to the Lions thanks to a late blitz of goals.

Official statements confirm that Millwall were in breach of FA Rule E21, which relates to a football club's responsibility to ensure its spectators and supporters (home and away) behave in an orderly fashion at matches.

Millwall have released a statement following the FA's punishment, where they have listed the sanctions they have faced for ableist and homophobic chanting towards Charlton.

Within that is confirmation that they have been handed a one-match partial stadium closure - the first time that an EFL club has been handed such a punishment from the FA.

The Athletic go on to confirm that it will be the Dockers Stand of the Den that will be impacted, with blocks 19, 20, 47 and 48 shut for the upcoming game against Sheffield United on December 8th.

That's going to impact a reported 1,274 fans who have tickets in that area, although they are invited to select an alternative seat in the stadium.

The additional one-match partial stadium closure that will be suspended until the end of next season will be activated if Millwall fans engage in more discriminatory chanting.

The statement from Millwall lays out what was chanted and why it was deemed unacceptable.

'South London S—' was the ableist chant, with 'You take it up the a—' the homophobic charge on the sanction.

Millwall's statement read: "Both chants are discriminatory and offensive, and the club condemns them in the strongest possible terms.

"Ableist and homophobic chanting, as well as any other form of discriminatory chanting, has no place in football or society. Any individual identified as engaging in such abuse will face the consequences."

Millwall's next home game comes on November 28th when they host Burnley in the EFL Championship.

Charlie Austin has opened up on the away dressing room at Millwall and how The Den could be a hostile venue for visitors.

#2081. What did the secret drone footage reveal about Manchester United training?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session was secretly filmed by a drone operator, who has since apologised and removed the footage from his YouTube channel after admitting his actions were unethical.

The footage showed players split into smaller groups carrying out different drills. On a separate full-size pitch, 11 players were positioned across the field alongside mannequins before gathering to receive instructions and feedback from new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Ten players were seen working with Pochettino in the video but only Harry Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo are regular starters among those.

Another group involved in drills was that of Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt, Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount, Leny Yoro, Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot.

In his statement, the operator said the flight itself was legal under drone regulations but accepted that recording the training session was wrong.

He explained that his intention was to give Manchester United supporters their first look at Pochettino wearing the club’s training kit.

He said: “A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.”

The operator apologized directly to the club, its new head coach and the players.

“I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.”

He also rejected any suggestion that Liverpool or another football club had been involved in his decision to film at Carrington.

“The video has been removed from my channel,” he added.

Netting 134 of his career goals at second tier level, the former striker knows exactly what it takes to be successful in the division both collectively and individually, as well as seeing the other side of the game at first-hand through an array of coaching and managerial roles.

Jamie Carragher believes Mauricio Pochettino has as much to prove as Manchester United, suggesting the Argentine’s reputation is not fully backed up by his achievements.

Mauricio Pochettino is preparing for his first match in charge of Manchester United against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, following his departure from the United States national team to replace Michael Carrick.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager has arrived at Old Trafford with plenty of experience, but Carragher believes his appointment represents an opportunity for both United and Pochettino to rebuild their reputations.

Writing in The Telegraph, the former Liverpool defender highlighted the irony of United turning to a manager whose own career needs a fresh start.

“It is ironic that in their latest attempt to rejuvenate and restore some of their old fire, Manchester United have turned to a manager whose career needs a similar reawakening,” Carragher wrote.

He suggested that Pochettino should be grateful that a club of United’s stature came calling at this stage of his career.

“Manchester United need a savior to first ease them from the relegation zone and then revive their Premier League and Champions League credibility. Pochettino, meanwhile, needed a club like United to save him from a managerial career that promised more than it delivered.”

Manchester United were fortunate to secure a manager with Pochettino’s experience after dismissing Michael Carrick so early in the season. However, he believes the Argentine has plenty to prove despite his strong reputation in the game.

“The South American returns to England with a big reputation, but not enough on his CV to back up glowing testimonials,” he continued.

Carrick believes one of the biggest concerns surrounding Pochettino is his record in important matches.

“A recurring issue with Pochettino, which continued with the US team, is an inability to get over the line in the most consequential, winnable matches, resulting in a lack of big trophies.”

Despite questioning his ability to bottle in big games, he praised his teams when everything comes in together.

“Ten years ago his best team were the embodiment of him, full of energy, style and ambition. Time will tell whether this version of Pochettino is the one turning up at Old Trafford.”

Pochettino will have the chance to shut Carragher’s doubts on Sunday when Manchester United face Liverpool. His immediate priority will be to take United out of the relegation zone, but the expectations at Old Trafford will extend far beyond survival.

The Liverpool fixture will be his first opportunity to make an impression. Carragher, however, believes the Argentine’s real challenge is to turn his reputation into success.

#2077. 'I couldn't understand' - Kim Hellberg reveals the 'biggest surprise' at Middlesbrough

Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg admitted that he "couldn't understand" how enormous the interest surrounding a football club in a specific town or city was before he came over to coach Boro last year.

The Swedish boss celebrated one year at the Riverside on Tuesday, and in that time, Middlesbrough have been transformed and look certain to be playing Premier League football in the near future.

Boro were inside the top two when Hellberg was hired, following the shock departure of Rob Edwards, but the brand of football he has instilled in the club has been thoroughly entertaining, both for fans of the club and neutrals alike.

Middlesbrough have a proud fanbase, and after years of Championship obscurity, they look to be on the rise again, and the energy surrounding the club from the fanbase is something that Hellberg has been surprised by during his first year on Teesside.

Kim Hellberg has seemed destined to coach in England ever since he started managing in Sweden a decade ago. But, as is often the case with foreign coaches, he was taken aback by the swell of support which surrounds football in this country.

It's tribalistic at times, and the fact that smaller cities and towns can have such a loyal, large following is always something that first-time coaches in this country take as a surprise. Hellberg is no different.

What's been your favourite moment from Kim Hellberg's first year in charge at Middlesbrough, Boro fans? Let us know in the comments.

To celebrate one year in charge at the Riverside, Middlesbrough ran a Q&A with their head coach, with him answering questions from fans. One such query regarded what has surprised him the most about Boro.

"I know football was everything here, but the biggest surprise for me was the enormous interest and energy around the football club," he said.

"How everyone feels like they care about Middlesbrough and live through that, how important football is wherever you go, wherever you are, football is everything here. I think I knew some bits were like that, but I couldn't understand how big it was."

Kim Hellberg will likely be referencing how most English clubs have such a passionate fanbase that lives through the team, but in Middlesbrough especially, that's evident.

Boro are a one-club town. No other professional team is in the Middlesbrough area, with the closest professional club being Hartlepool United, 13 miles away. Even then, those in Hartlepool count themselves more in County Durham, rather than Teesside.

Either way, it's a proud following at Boro, and has been for years. Their time in the Premier League grew that, but even in the past few years, attendances at the Riverside have hovered around the 25,000 mark in the Championship.

All you have to do is look at the numbers over the past year to know that Kim Hellberg is bringing back some of the supporter base who may have become a little disassociated with the club as they stagnated in the second tier, though.

Boro's lowest Saturday attendance this season was against Cardiff City, at 28,991. Their average attendance in the entirety of last season was 27,622, and the year before, in Michael Carrick's final term, it was 25,416.

Over 3,000 more fans are coming to watch this Middlesbrough team under Hellberg than they were in the final moments of the Carrick reign, which shows how much bigger an already big support has been under Hellberg.

Hellberg went on to say that his dream as Boro boss was to bring the club back to the Premier League, which he hopes to do this season.

Middlesbrough currently sit atop the Championship table, and look good value for it, too. What's arguably more scary, though, is that they seem to still have a higher gear that they can reach, and if they can find it, they may win this league at a canter.

Football League World has named and ranked the SEVEN best young EFL managers right now with a strict 40-or-under criteria

Then, the Swedish boss may end up being taken further aback by the extra support which will come at the top level. Boro are a club that has been starved of Premier League football, with this being the 17th of the last 18 seasons they've spent in the Championship.

You get the feeling, though, that if Hellberg can get this side into the top flight, they'll stand a greater chance of staying there than they did under Aitor Karanka a decade ago.

The Bruno Fernandes contract situation comes at a difficult time for United, who are 18th in the Premier League with eight points from their opening 10 matches. They have managed just one win and five draws during that run.

Pochettino has inherited a struggling side, and keeping Bruno Fernandes committed to the project could prove important as he is one of the few performing stars in the fragile Manchester United team.

#2075. Liverpool vs Man Utd: Preview, key stats, team news & where to watch

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Mauricio Pochettino begins his Manchester United reign with a huge test at Anfield on Sunday, with Manchester United desperate for a result after making their worst start to a top-flight season in 40 years.

Manchester United have collected just eight points from their opening 10 Premier League matches, with one win and five draws leaving them 18th in the table. They have also conceded in every league game this season and are currently on a run of 11 consecutive matches without keeping a clean sheet in all competitions.

Mauricio Pochettino only arrived to the club on Wednesday after replacing Michael Carrick, leaving him with just a few training sessions to prepare for one of the biggest fixtures in English football.

There is some encouragement for the Argentine, however. Eight of United’s last nine permanent or caretaker managers have avoided defeat in their first match in charge. That may be some encouragement to the Argentine.

Meanwhile, Liverpool are not exactly enjoying a comfortable season at home either. They sit fourth with 18 points but have won just once in their five Premier League matches at Anfield so far, giving them the third-worst home record in the Premier League.

Their recent form across all competitions stands at three wins, one draw and two defeats in their last six matches. Liverpool most recently beat Crystal Palace 3-1, but they will know that United’s poor league position does not make this fixture any less complicated.

Liverpool have received positive news ahead of Sunday’s meeting. Dominik Szoboszlai and Virgil van Dijk are both expected to feature, while Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong could also be available.

Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni have returned to team training following knee injuries but are unlikely to make the squad. Hugo Ekitike remains a long-term absentee with an Achilles problem.

Manchester United could welcome back Patrick Dorgu and Harry Maguire after both trained following fitness concerns. They were seen in that leaked drone footage as well. Lisandro Martínez is also available again after serving his suspension.

Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford could return, although their availability remains uncertain. Carlos Baleba, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko are still sidelined.

The new United boss has a difficult personal record against Liverpool. Pochettino has faced the Reds 19 times, winning three, drawing five and losing 11. He has also failed to win any of his last eight meetings with them in all competitions. That might be a concern, but everything has a first time.

Pochettino will be encouraged by United’s overall record against Liverpool.  United have an edge with 85 wins compared to Liverpool’s 72 across 218 meetings. Their most recent encounter also went their way, with a 3-2 victory on May 3.

However, United arrive on a disappointing run of seven consecutive away matches without a win and have managed just one victory in their last 11 games.

#2074. Rangers & Simon Jordan won’t like what’s happening at Leicester City right now

Leicester City and Russell Martin are in far better form, with Rangers and Simon Jordan now part of an interesting story developing in recent months now that things are finally looking up for the Foxes.

Their 1-0 away victory over Huddersfield Town was arguably one of the most impressive results anywhere in League One this season, suggesting Russell Martin's ideas are beginning to take hold with this Leicester City squad.

The former MK Dons, Swansea City, Southampton, and Rangers boss has now taken charge of five clubs, with Leicester representing his latest challenge. After a difficult start, he is beginning to show why the Foxes appointed him.

Martin's appointment at Leicester was always going to divide opinion, particularly after his disastrous 123-day spell at Rangers, where he won just five of his 17 matches before being dismissed.

He then endured a difficult start in the East Midlands, winning two and losing three of his first eight league fixtures. The pressure was considerable given Leicester's expectation of bouncing straight back to the Championship, with another season in League One representing a disaster for a club of their stature.

Simon Jordan was among those questioning Martin's position at Leicester, with things looking particularly bleak after the 3-1 defeat to Peterborough United and former Leicester player Robbie Savage. The warning was there that he would be sacked unless results improved.

The 25 top scorers in the Championship since the second tier was rebranded back in 2004/05, including Billy Sharp and Aleksandar Mitrovic.

However, the Foxes have since won four of their next six league games, including that outstanding Huddersfield victory. Rangers supporters and some of the divisive coach’s other critics could be eating their words.

They have always piled on Martin for last season, with neither they nor Jordan perhaps enjoying seeing him turn things around. Leicester are looking considerably more positive, easy on the eye, and results are following.

Martin's Southampton side also took time to get going, suffering four consecutive defeats early in his first season before eventually embarking on a remarkable 25-match unbeaten run.

George Elek, an EFL expert and Not The Top 20 podcast pundit, has argued that Martin's reputation has become a footballing culture war, with his failures often attracting considerably more attention than his achievements.

Will Russell Martin return Leicester to the Championship at the first time of asking? Comment below!

In further replies on X (formerly Twitter), Elek added: "Tough ask to expect him to come on board a sinking ship and turn it around straight away. League position at this stage is pretty meaningless, they’re clearly playing well now. Why do you think chucking money at it will solve the clear rot that had set in? His playing style is extreme. Is he not entitled to have some time to implement it?"

There is a reasonable argument that Leicester simply needed to give him time to implement his ideas, particularly given the scale of the rebuilding job. The Foxes could now be ready to climb the table rapidly and become genuine automatic promotion contenders rather than simply hoping to sneak into the play-offs.

There is, however, a cautionary tale from Martin's Southampton tenure. Despite that extraordinary unbeaten run, Saints eventually fizzled out during the closing stages of the 2023/24 campaign, losing three games in one damaging April week and missing out on automatic promotion.

They entered the play-offs with questions surrounding their form, although they ultimately overcame Leeds at Wembley. Leicester would happily take that outcome, but should be wary of allowing their standards to drop once the initial momentum arrives.

Martin has the midfield quality to dominate League One for the foreseeable future, with John Lundstram, Sammy Braybrooke, Will Smallbone, and Louis Page offering an excellent blend of technical ability, energy and composure.

That engine room could become the foundation of a serious promotion challenge from this point forth. Rangers fans and Jordan would not enjoy that turnaround, should it come to fruition.

#2073. Why can Mauricio Pochettino turn things around at Manchester United?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of his first United game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, with plenty of questions surrounding the players who will benefit from his arrival.

Manchester United have struggled badly this season, sitting 18th in the Premier League after collecting just eight points from their opening 10 matches.

Pochettino replaces Michael Carrick and his job has been described as one of the toughest jobs in the Premier League. Former defender Wes Brown believes Manchester United have a chance with Pochettino to change things despite it being very difficult.

Brown believes the new manager has enough quality at his disposal to improve the situation, despite the difficult start and the pressure that comes with the Manchester United job.

Asked whether Pochettino faces an impossible task after previous managers failed to bring success to Old Trafford, Brown was confident the Argentine could make a difference.

“Definitely not impossible. Regardless of what has happened so far this season, Manchester United do have good players,” Wes Brown said while talking to Flashscore.

Brown expects Pochettino to demand more effort from the squad.

“He looks like a personable manager, so can work with these players individually to get their confidence up and really play for the shirt and create that positive vibe that seems to be missing.”

Asked about how long Manchester United will take to be a title challenger again, Wes Brown was cautious in putting any numbers.

“Well, it isn’t going to happen overnight. You will need a reaction quickly, that is for sure. They are very far away, but you have to start with consistency and that is something Pochettino has to install and deliver a consistency of play, to be fitter than your opponent and show fight.”

The former defender also highlighted Bruno Fernandes’ drop in form, suggesting the captain could benefit from a change in management.

“You have to see Bruno’s form has dropped, so it will be great to see this pick up under the new manager.”

Pochettino’s priority will be getting a response on Sunday against Liverpool from his senior players. United have been in this cycle of repeating managers and not finding much success. Mauricio Pochettino needs to take things one at a time. Sunday would be that first step.

#2072. Manchester United managerial costs near £100m as Pochettino fee revealed

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. Manchester United have spent approximately £95m appointing and dismissing managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013, according to BBC Sport, with the total expected to pass £100m following Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival.

United’s latest financial disclosures confirm a fee of £7.584m in connection with appointing Pochettino, who left his role as United States national team head coach earlier this month.

The figure takes the cumulative cost of managerial changes to around £95m, according to BBC Sport’s analysis. That total is expected to rise once the costs of Michael Carrick’s dismissal and appointing Pochettino’s coaching staff are included.

Pochettino signed a two-and-a-half-year contract on 13 November, replacing Carrick after a difficult start to the Premier League season. The club’s Stock Market filing states that the appointment fee will be recognised in its financial accounts for the current quarter. United also confirmed borrowing a further £10m on 16 November, taking the amount drawn on their revolving credit facility to £240m.

Pochettino is United’s ninth full-time managerial appointment since Ferguson’s departure, including Ralf Rangnick’s interim spell. The club have also changed managers during each of the past three seasons.

United’s financial disclosures show that their long-term debt stood at £577.4m on 30 September, while outstanding transfer-fee commitments totalled £417m. Those figures are separate from the cost of appointing and dismissing managers.

A Reuters analysis has put the wider cost of managerial and senior football staff changes above £100m, using a broader calculation. Pochettino now faces the task of improving United’s results, beginning with Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool.

EFL pundits Callum Fowler and Jimmy Smith have issued a warning to the Plymouth Argyle hierarchy after Tom Cleverley's side were defeated 2-0 by Peterborough United at Home Park without the attacking quality of Canadian forward, Bim Pepple.

Argyle's positive start to the League One season has hit stumbling block, with the home defeat to Robbie Savage's side following a heavy 3-0 defeat to Sheffield Wednesday at Hillsborough.

Harry Leonard's goal put the seal on things for Posh after his namesake, Harry Ashfield, opened the scoring midway through the first period.

Other results meant the Green Army dropped to seventh in the table, having taken 23 points from their opening 16 matches.

However, the growing concern surrounding Cleverley's men is their transfer strategy and lack of potential strength-in-depth, with the former Manchester United and England midfielder opting for a front two of Will Evans and Caleb Watts, with Pepple absent for just a third time this campaign.

Pepple moved to Home Park from Luton Town last summer in a deal which could rise as high as £600k, with the former Chesterfield loanee netting 16 times in just 35 League One appearances for the Pilgrims last term as Cleverley's men narrowly missed out on the play-offs.

The 23-year-old has scored five times so far this term, but was sidelined before the defeat to Sheffield Wednesday with a muscular issue.

Regardless, Cleverley backed his fellow attackers to step up to the plate and provide goals, but with blanks fired in the past 180 minutes' worth of action, questions have arisen on this particular front.

Pepple was one half of Argyle's formidable attacking duo last season, with Lorent Tolaj finding the net 21 times in his 35 appearances for the club, before the Swiss youth international was sold to Bristol City in a £4m deal.

Plymouth then sought to replace the 25-year-old with Evans, who is yet to replicate his prior Mansfield Town exploits after a £400,000 agreement, having netted just three times whilst starting in all of his new employers' 16 league encounters.

Discussing a potential overreliance on Pepple, Fowler said on the Pyramid podcast: "They've got some good players, but they're screaming out for a 'proper' forward.

"Pepple didn't play in this (game). He's not there.

"So, from what were your starting strikers last season in Tolaj and Pepple, both brilliant for this level. They've got Evans and Watts," he added.

"That's where your problem is, it's a lack of quality," Fowler claimed.

The concerns raised by Fowler and Smith are particularly valid, both in the short and long-term, as it remains to be seen when Pepple returns from injury, as well as where he is playing his football in the coming months.

When building a squad it is important to have a vision of the end goal, and AC Milan have exactly that heading into 2027.

La Gazzetta dello Sport begin a report by stating that there are no transition years when it comes to Milan. Frequently they have chosen to overhaul the squad in the summer window, and sometimes even in the winter.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For example, 2024 brought Paulo Fonseca with Morata, Pavlovic, Fofana, Emerson Royal, Jimenez and Abraham. Then, 2025 brought Gimenez, then Massimiliano Allegri with Modric, Rabiot, Nkunku, Jashari, and De Winter. Last summer brought Ruben Amorim with Ramos, Moreira, Gila, and Cisse.

A not-so-bold prediction: 2027 won’t be slow. Gerry Cardinale even hinted at this, stating: “We’ll continue to be aggressive and opportunistic. It will take a couple more transfer windows to complete everything.” The two transfer windows? Winter and summer, 2027.

The Rossoneri have two key needs right now: a striker and a central defender. They’ll try to secure them as early as the month after next. Nicolo Tresoldi and Endrick are the names that have been talked about for weeks, but the transfer market has surprises.

The difficulties are well known: Club Brugge do not want to sell their jewel in January unless a €60m check materialises, while with Endrick it seems the will of Jose Mourinho must be taken into account. So, alternative names could emerge for the attack.

A central defender is less of a pressing need. Eight months ago, Milan decided to explore the possibility of signing Virgil van Dijk, who turned 35 in July and is regarded as one of the best of his generation.

A year ago, the conditions weren’t there, but now they might be. Van Dijk’s contract expires in June and he’s always been fascinated by Milan and Italy. It’s complex, but it’s worth a try, and Cardinale seems to agree.

Then there is Gabriele Calvani. He’s Italian, 22, plays for Frosinone, and is expected to start San Siro on Sunday. The Diavolo are interested, just as they are keen on Sporting CP’s Gonçalo Inacio, whom Amorim has already coached and attempted to sign in the summer.

Milan will undoubtedly make some changes to their bench over the next 12 months, aiming to mix young players with experienced players. Filippo Terracciano will leave in January, Vladimirov needs to play, Hutchinson is on loan until June, and Jashari will have to reconsider his future.

It’s certain that some Diawara-like players will arrive, i.e. promising prospects chosen through scouting and data. Markus Krösche – if he becomes the new Head of Football, as is now almost certain – will have extensive powers in this regard.

The idea of ​​making the team more Italian is there, but we know how the market works, making it difficult to plan. Not only that, but some Italians will soon leave Milan too. Above all, Christian Comotto and Francesco Camarda are heading out on loan.

The former seems destined for Daniele De Rossi’s Genoa, while it remains to be seen where and under what terms the altter will leave. A loan with an option to buy, leaving Milan free to control the future, probably. To a small Serie A team? Possibly, but a move abroad is possible too.

Belgium and the Netherlands are countries where strikers historically have more opportunities in teams that are younger, while Germany could be another destination. If he takes a flight north, don’t be surprised.

#2068. Bruno Fernandes breaks silence on Man Utd contract offer

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Bruno Fernandes has been Manchester United’s most creative player since his arrival to the club in 2020.

The 32-year-old is approaching the final months of his current deal, which expires at the end of the season. United do have the option to extend his contract by another 12 months, keeping him at Old Trafford until 2028.

While they can extend his contract for a year, Manchester United are actively pursuing a deal to tie Bruno Fernandes beyond 2028.

Bruno Fernandes himself has now confirmed that the club have offered him a new contract, but the midfielder has made it clear that he does not want discussions about his future to become a priority right now.

Fernandes confirmed that an offer had been made but dismissed suggestions that he was holding out for a better salary or a longer agreement.

“The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay,” he told Sky Sports.

He also insisted that money has never been the reason behind his decision to remain at United, despite having opportunities to move elsewhere in previous transfer windows.

“If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here,” Fernandes said.

The Portugal international added that he could have earned considerably more by accepting offers from other clubs, but always chose to continue his career in Manchester.

Fernandes revealed that discussions initially took place towards the end of last season and continued when the players returned for pre-season.

However, the United captain believes the current situation at the club makes it the wrong time to focus on his personal future.

“We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side,” he explained.

“I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.”

Fernandes has been one of United’s most influential players since arriving from Sporting in 2020. He has scored 75 Premier League goals for the club and set a new competition record for assists in a single season last term.

Bruno’s comments don’t sound like he is holding United hostage demanding more pay or refusing to sign a new one. The intention as told by Bruno Fernandes just show his leadership trait about putting the team first. He has no immediate intention of making his contract situation the centre of attention. That will be a sign of encouragement for the fans as well.

Manchester United need to start winning games again. When they do and surely Bruno Fernandes will be at the centre of it, the contract talks can resume and take priority.

The Swedish head coach also revealed that Rangers loanee Connor Barron is currently injured, but with no minutes in a Boro shirt since his arrival in the summer, it's almost all but certain that the Scottish giants will be considering bringing him back once the window opens.

Speaking after their 2-0 win over Bristol City last Saturday, Hellberg said that it was "absolute" that Middlesbrough needed to strengthen their midfield, with it likely that Sebastian Berhalter and Aidan Morris will be their only senior central midfielders come the end of the calendar year.

Here are three players they should be targetting.

We'll start with arguably the more underwhelming choice, but one that would ensure continuity and familiarity within the squad and wouldn't put too much pressure on replacing Morris or Berhalter, who are becoming quite an established duo in the engine room.

Alan Browne spent last season on loan at Middlesbrough from Sunderland, playing the utility role to perfection. The Irishman played a range of positions in midfield and even covered across the backline when needed.

Various injuries to key players effectively made him a first-choice player from mid-January until the end of the season, and he played the full 90 minutes in their play-off final defeat to Hull City back in May.

Since returning to the Stadium of Light, Browne hasn't featured in competitions that the Black Cats care about. His only bows have come in the EFL Cup and the EFL Trophy. He's yet to make a squad in the Europa League, and finally made his first Premier League 20 in their goalless draw with Aston Villa on Saturday.

There were murmurs back in September about him possibly having his contract paid out, and if Boro could bring him back for free, he'd be a useful addition.

Even so, with his deal set to expire in the summer, the 31-year-old shouldn't be available for too much in January if he's still under contract on Wearside.

Barnsley are in some real dire straits at the moment, battling down at the bottom of League One.

January will be crucial if Daniel Stendel's side are going to avoid a first fourth-tier campaign since the late 1970s, but there's the possibility that they could be looking even worse come the time the window slams shut.

Despite the Tykes' position, they still have some quality amongst the squad, and there's a strong possibility that the unpopular ownership group at Oakwell could cash in on the likes of Reyes Cleary or, in this case, Patrick Kelly, as they'd be worth a lot less as League Two footballers in the summer if that's where they end up.

Football League World has named and ranked the SEVEN best young EFL managers right now with a strict 40-or-under criteria

Cleary gets a lot of the plaudits amongst neutrals, given how impressive he was last season, but, arguably, Kelly has been Barnsley's best player so far this term.

The Northern Irish international has run the show from midfield. Only Derensili Sanches Fernandes and Oliver Norwood have created more chances from open play in League One, and only the Huddersfield Town wideman and Will Alves have created more chances as a result of them carrying the ball forward.

Kelly has excelled in the high-octane, pressing style that Stendel has deployed at Barnsley this season, so he shouldn't have to adapt too much to what Hellberg would want him to do, which may have been the issue for Leo Castledine this time last season.

And as a chance creator, he could deputise in the Riley McGree role behind the striker if needs be, too.

Middlesbrough have found joy in scouting from the MLS and looking at American midfielders, so if a new middle-man is needed at the Riverside in January, it wouldn't be wild to take a look at some of the better-performing Americans in the division in 2026.

17-year-old Adri Mehmeti would be a dream signing by the looks of things, but realistically, whoever comes in will likely initially be playing understudy to their two compatriots already in the middle at the Riverside.

23-year-old Beau Leroux of the San Jose Earthquakes could be considered, though. The defensive midfielder initially looks like a bit of a disruptor, like Morris can be.

Do you think there are other MLS gems who Middlesbrough could target this January? Let us know in the comments.

The Boro man has made more tackles and won possession more times than anyone in the Championship so far this season, per Opta. In the 2026 MLS campaign, Leroux was 8th in duels won, 10th in possession won and 25th in tackles made.

Per FotMob, the 23-year-old was a top 10% defensive midfielder in defensive contributions, recoveries and possession won in the final third, and in the top 1% for duels won.

So, defensively, he looks to be a strong candidate, but he can also bring something in the attacking and chance-creating sense, too. He scored four and assisted seven in 33 MLS games last season, taking 52 shots from defensive midfield and creating 37 chances.

Leroux's ceiling looks quite high, and there is room for improvement. His pass percentage numbers weren't much to shout about, so if he does come in, he would seemingly be someone to learn from Morris and Berhalter, who look to do either side of the game better than he does right now.

However, if he can realise his potential under Helberg, he could become a real all-action box-to-box midfielder who could cope with the Premier League, which is Middlesbrough's ultimate goal come the end of this season.

#2065. Liverpool v Manchester United: Five classic wins at Anfield

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

From Diego Forlan’s unforgettable double to Juan Mata’s spectacular volley, Manchester United have enjoyed some memorable victories at Anfield over the years.

With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.

United travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory. Instead, centre-back Gary Pallister scored twice with headers from David Beckham deliveries, either side of John Barnes’s equaliser.

Andy Cole added a third after the interval, heading home from Gary Neville’s cross following an error by Liverpool goalkeeper David James. The victory helped Sir Alex Ferguson’s side take a decisive step towards retaining the Premier League title, which they secured the following month.

Fresh from winning the Treble, United returned to Anfield for a remarkable match in September 1999. Jamie Carragher headed into his own net inside three minutes before Andy Cole doubled United’s advantage.

Sami Hyypia pulled a goal back for Liverpool, but Carragher’s second own goal restored the visitors’ two-goal lead. Patrik Berger reduced the deficit again, and United faced a difficult finish after Cole was sent off for a second bookable offence. Despite playing the closing stages with 10 men, Ferguson’s side held on for a 3-2 victory.

Diego Forlan had endured a frustrating start to his United career before producing a performance that supporters would remember for years. The Uruguayan opened the scoring after Liverpool goalkeeper Jerzy Dudek failed to gather the ball, allowing him to finish from close range.

Forlan added a second just minutes later, beating Dudek at his near post to put United in control. Sami Hyypia pulled one back for Liverpool, but Ferguson’s side held on for a victory that proved valuable in their successful pursuit of the 2002-03 Premier League title. Forlan’s double also inspired a terrace song that remains familiar to United supporters.

Few United victories at Anfield have been as dramatic as the one secured by John O’Shea in March 2007. Liverpool had enjoyed the better opportunities, and United’s task became harder when Paul Scholes was sent off late in the second half.

With a goalless draw appearing increasingly likely, Cristiano Ronaldo’s free-kick was parried by goalkeeper Pepe Reina. Substitute O’Shea reacted quickest, firing the rebound high into the net in stoppage time. The unexpected winner gave United three valuable points on their way to reclaiming the Premier League title.

Juan Mata produced one of the most memorable individual performances in this fixture during Louis van Gaal’s first season as United manager. The Spaniard opened the scoring after 14 minutes, finishing a move involving Ander Herrera, before doubling United’s lead with a spectacular scissor-kick volley after half-time.

Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard had been sent off just 38 seconds after coming on as a substitute at the interval. Daniel Sturridge reduced the deficit, while Wayne Rooney missed a late penalty, but United held on for a 2-1 victory. Mata’s second goal remains one of the outstanding moments of United’s Premier League visits to Anfield.

Those five victories underline the different ways United have succeeded at Anfield, from outstanding individual performances to late winners and determined defensive displays. Pochettino now has an opportunity to begin his managerial reign with a memorable result against United’s biggest rivals.

Which United victory at Anfield is your favourite? Were you there for Forlan’s double, O’Shea’s winner or Mata’s volley? Share your memories in the comments below.

#2062. Manchester United’s 34-goal defensive record shows scale of Pochettino’s task

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Manchester United have conceded more goals than any other club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues this season, underlining the scale of the challenge facing Mauricio Pochettino following Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

Pochettino’s first match in charge ended in a heavy defeat at Anfield after defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute. Although the dismissal left United facing an uphill struggle, their defensive record suggests the new head coach has inherited problems that extend well beyond one match.

According to an analysis published by the Premier League, United have conceded 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions this season. That is the highest total of any club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues, with Sunday’s defeat adding four more goals to an already concerning record.

The Premier League also calculated Liverpool’s expected goals at 4.38, suggesting the hosts created enough chances to have won by an even greater margin. United’s difficulties began when Matthijs de Ligt misjudged a long ball, and Yoro fouled Alexander Isak as the Liverpool forward attempted to break through on goal.

Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick, with Florian Wirtz doubling Liverpool’s advantage just three minutes later. Rio Ngumoha and substitute Victor Munoz completed the scoring after half-time.

The defeat left United 19th in the Premier League, with just eight points from their opening 11 matches and one league victory all season. Pochettino acknowledged the painful nature of the result but argued that the early dismissal had transformed the contest. He also questioned whether Yoro should have been sent off, given the circumstances of the challenge on Isak.

The Argentine’s first tactical plan was disrupted almost immediately, making it difficult to draw firm conclusions about how United might perform under him with a full complement of players.

Nevertheless, the defensive record accumulated before his arrival makes clear that improving the team’s organisation will be a central part of his work. The Premier League’s analysis highlighted De Ligt’s mistake before the sending-off and the opportunities Liverpool continued to create against United’s depleted defence.

United return to Champions League action on Wednesday when they travel to Portugal to face Sporting, giving Pochettino little time to address the issues exposed at Anfield. The fixture offers an early opportunity to assess how he intends to organise his defence and whether the team can respond to another damaging result.

Pochettino must also decide how to balance defensive stability with the need to improve results. United’s league position means they cannot afford to spend too long finding that balance. The circumstances of Sunday’s defeat were unusual, and the red card undoubtedly made United’s task more difficult. But conceding 34 goals in 16 matches points to a wider problem that will require sustained improvement rather than a reaction to one result.

For Pochettino, making United harder to beat is an obvious starting point. Wednesday’s trip to Sporting will provide his next opportunity to begin that process.

#2059. Roy Keane questions Manchester United standards after Liverpool humiliation

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Former Manchester United captain Roy Keane has criticised the players’ performance and questioned supporters applauding them after Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, insisting the early red card was no excuse for the manner of the loss.

Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge unravelled when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes at Anfield. Liverpool scored twice inside 13 minutes and added two more goals after the break, leaving United 19th in the Premier League.

Speaking on Sky Sports, Keane challenged the suggestion that United’s performance was understandable because they had played most of the match with 10 men.

“Fans are applauding. Applauding what?” he asked, before describing the performance as “rubbish”.

Keane argued that United should have shown greater fight and quality, claiming Liverpool could have scored eight or nine goals. He also questioned why responsibility for the club’s problems so often fell on managers, owners and executives rather than the players themselves.

Some travelling supporters applauded the team after the final whistle, potentially recognising the difficulty of playing more than 80 minutes with a numerical disadvantage. Keane, however, viewed the reaction as evidence of declining expectations.

Keane also challenged fellow former United captain Gary Neville, who had suggested the early dismissal made the result more understandable. Neville was far from satisfied with United’s performance, though, and separately accused the club’s hierarchy of negligence for failing to strengthen the defence.

The disagreement reflected two concerns surrounding United: the players’ response to adversity and the quality of the squad available to Pochettino. Liverpool’s goals came from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz, with the hosts creating numerous further opportunities.

Pochettino defended his players’ commitment afterwards and questioned Yoro’s dismissal, arguing that Alexander Isak had not established control of the ball when the defender challenged him. United have taken just eight points from 11 Premier League matches, leaving their new manager with little time to improve results. They travel to Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday before returning to domestic action.

Keane’s criticism adds to the scrutiny surrounding the squad following another heavy defeat to their fiercest rivals. For Pochettino, the immediate challenge is to improve defensive organisation while restoring confidence in a side struggling near the bottom of the table.

#2058. Chelsea World Cup Knockout Load Gives Xabi Alonso Pre-Season Problem

Chelsea’s World Cup contingent has moved from a group-stage watchlist into a genuine Xabi Alonso planning problem.

Chelsea’s own tournament update confirms that Enzo Fernandez, Mike Penders, Moises Caicedo, Kendry Paez, Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato have reached the Round of 32.

England have also progressed after their final Group L win over Panama, which keeps Reece James and Trevoh Chalobah inside the wider knockout picture.

For supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

The concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

Those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Instead, the players most central to that reset are still operating in knockout football.

Caicedo’s Ecuador role is the cleanest example. Read Chelsea has already assessed how his captaincy display against Germany strengthened his leadership case, but the next layer is more complicated.

Every additional knockout tie gives him more tournament rhythm, more authority and more fatigue.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring issue ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to plan around a large World Cup group.

The broader issue was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

Enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine issue, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

Caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

That is where the James situation feels central.

If Chelsea’s captain carries a World Cup hamstring warning, the club’s right-sided structure becomes more than a selection debate.

It becomes an availability question that touches Gusto, the wider defensive rebuild and the need for control from midfield.

Read Chelsea has already looked at James’ captaincy test under Alonso, and the injury layer now makes that test sharper.

This is the hidden cost of a strong international footprint.

Chelsea want players good enough to survive deep into tournaments.

Alonso now has to make sure that status does not leave his first league weeks short of the very control those players are meant to provide.

#2057. Derby County fans slammed for "utterly ridiculous" David Clowes claims

Despite pushing the Championship play-off places close in 2025-26, Derby County have been one of the big strugglers of the current campaign.

The Rams finished just four points adrift of the top six in May, but despite the backing in the transfer window of manager John Eustace, who was able to spend money on the likes of Bobby Clark, David Ozoh and Alex Mowatt, has struggled to get a tune out of his squad.

Injuries of course have not helped matters at Pride Park, but they sit inside the second tier relegation zone with Burnley and Preston North End, with no end in sight to their struggles.

Whilst the fanbase has been divided on Eustace's role as manager, with some wanting him gone and others blaming injuries for their rotten form as of late, chairman David Clowes is now getting it in the neck.

Local businessman Clowes rescued County in 2022 from administration, not long before they were close to liquidation after failing to find a buyer for some months, and just two years later, Derby were back in the Championship.

Clowes has made no secret about his search for external investment, but with Turki Alalshikh's buyout collapsing in August, it's left the 57-year-old on his own again.

And some Derby fans, like this one via X, are calling for Clowes to sell the club and depart to allow someone else to take them forward.

Whilst another believes that sticking with Eustace as manager and the results that have followed means that Clowes is ruining the legacy that he created a few years ago.

It's fair to say though that not every Rams fan is in agreement with the complaints and criticism that Clowes is getting.

When asked on the current situation at Pride Park right now, Football League World's Derby fan pundit, Shaun Woodward, believes that Clowes is getting an unnecessarily hard time from the fans.

"Some of the criticism David Clowes is receiving online is utterly ridiculous," Shaun told FLW.

"I'm not going to say that he should be immune to it, because he is the chairman of the club, and when a team is doing badly, the finger is going to be pointed at the manager and the chairman, it comes with the territory. I'm not going to sit here and say he should be immune from ever having any negativity thrown at him. We can't forever say because he saved the club, he's got a free pass, so to speak.

"But, the guy is a legend at Derby, and I do believe he deserves a little bit more respect on his name.

Clowes has Woodward's backing at Derby, and likely thousands of other fans, as it's not too long ago that he took a big risk to bring them out of liquidation danger.

But it's clear to see that everything is not alright on the pitch. County are struggling to pick up points, and to the surprise of many from the start of the season that would've predicted them to be challenging for the top eight.

Many clubs would have changed manager by now, and whether or not Clowes is sticking by him or is being indecisive is a matter of opinion, but Woodward believes he needs to make the big call as soon as possible - whilst also being thankful that Clowes isn't another Mel Morris who throws his money around unnecessarily.

Who are the most hated Championship fanbases? The Supercomputer tells all...

"Yes, he's making mistakes right now, and I do believe he should be getting rid of John Eustace, Stephen Pearce and quite a lot of the backroom staff - they don't seem to be doing their jobs," Shaun admitted.

"He should be surrounding himself with better footballing people that will make better decisions either with him or for him."

"Who knows what is going on behind the scenes, I don't know whether he's actively out there trying to find those people, but it does seem at the moment that he is struggling to make a decision, and the longer we stay in this no man's land, where Pearce and Eustace are still around and we are losing every week, he's going to take a lot of flak.

"I still believe we should be thankful for what we have, and some of our fans have got short memories. We don't want to go back to the days of a Mel Morris-type chairman, who on the surface looked great by bringing in all these players, but behind the scenes he was lowering the club into the ground.

Does David Clowes need to sack John Eustace at Derby County? Comment below!

"It's frustrating right now results-wise, but that to me is on John Eustace. I think Clowes has backed him the best he can, but he's probably struggling to make that big call about whether he should fire him or not, and I do feel for him.

But ultimately he's got to start making these big calls sooner rather than later, or he will continue to get some stick, but some of it is ridiculous in my opinion, and it needs to stop."

#2056. Manchester United to appeal Leny Yoro red card as Fernandes questions officials

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Manchester United have notified the Football Association of their intention to appeal against Leny Yoro’s red card during Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, with captain Bruno Fernandes among those questioning the decision.

The French defender was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak outside the penalty area. Referee Sam Barrott ruled that Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity, with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from the resulting free-kick.

According to Sky Sports, United intend to challenge the decision, with Isak’s chances of regaining possession central to the dispute. Mauricio Pochettino questioned whether Isak would have reached the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens, a view shared by midfielder Kobbie Mainoo.

Fernandes told the BBC after the match that it was “never a red card”.

“To make a mistake like this can change a game,” he said, as reported by the Press Association. The Portuguese midfielder nevertheless accepted that United were responsible for conceding from the subsequent free-kick.

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher offered a different assessment on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch programme, supporting Barrott’s decision while acknowledging the uncertainty over whether Isak would have reached the ball before Lammens.

“I think most people would have expected a red card,” Gallagher said.

An attacker’s likelihood of retaining or regaining possession is among the factors referees must consider when assessing whether a foul has denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

United host Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday in Pochettino’s first home match in charge. Unless the appeal succeeds, Yoro will serve a one-match suspension against the Bees. United sit 19th in the Premier League, having won just one of their opening 11 matches. Yoro remains eligible for Wednesday’s Champions League fixture against Sporting, before attention turns to a crucial domestic fixture for Pochettino’s side.
