#1991. GdS: Cisse becomes a pillar as Amorim as experiments with four-man attack

Alphadjo Cisse has definitely been the breakout player of the season so far and Ruben Amorim has no intention of dialling down his presence in attack.

Milan had a very clear plan when they headed into the current season: Goncalo Ramos would be the main man in attack. Instead, however, it’s the underdog Cisse who has been running the show, while the Portuguese striker has been at the bottom in terms of output.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning (see image below), that’s why there cannot be – and likely won’t be – a Milan without Cisse in attack. Ruben Amorim now wants to build the attack around him, as opposed to introducing him every now and then.

The most recent clash, the 2-1 win against Genoa, was a good example of this. Amorim went for a bold formation with Cisse, Ramos, Christian Pulisic, Diego Moreira, Luka Modric and Adrien Rabiot together. A team with a lot of quality and an attacking-minded style.

It was a shape that reminded us of 2009-10, when Milan were guided by another foreign coach: Leonardo. He chose a very attacking-minded side with four attackers and two midfielders, which is something that Amorim almost replicated.

Modric and Rabiot in front of the defence (Pirlo and Ambrosini then) and the fantasy project with Pulisic, Moreira, Cisse, and Ramos, comparable to the Ronaldinho, Pato, Seedorf, and Borriello of the old days.

Despite this, the goals were scored after two mistakes by Genoa (even if Milan’s pressing helped), so the goal is to repeat the experiment against Frosinone and to increase its effectiveness, the experiment should be repeated tomorrow.

In that sense, Cisse will be important as he’s the top scorer: three goals in Europa League and five in Serie A. He has scored with both feet and his head, demonstrating a combination of talent and an eye for goal: characteristics that are very important for a team like Milan.

The average also speaks for itself: eight goals spread across 658 minutes means he scores a goal every 82 minutes.  Best of all, his versatility means that he can play as an attacking midfielder, a left-winger, and even as a centre-forward.

At just 20 years and 17 days old, thanks to the fifth goal in his ninth Serie A appearance, Cisse became the second-youngest player to reach the milestone in the first ten games with Milan, at least since 1994-95. Only Pato did it younger, at 18 years and 181 days.

Furthermore, he’s one of only three players born after 2006 (top five leagues) to have scored eight or more goals in all competitions, along with Lamine Yamal (13) and Paris Brunner, who also scored eight.

As the pink newspaper concludes, Ramos has also produced eye-catching numbers, but in this case in a negative sense: 1,191 minutes on the pitch, three goals scored, meaning one goal scored every 398 minutes.

#1989. Man City vs. Napoli: How to watch Champions League clash, date, time, live stream, TV channel

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 09:20

Gameweek five in the Champions League sees Manchester City and Napoli square off in the League Phase.

These two teams suffered contrasting results in the previous round of fixtures, and here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into to their latest encounter.

Man City vs. Napoli will kick off at 20:00 UK time on Tuesday night.

This contest is one of nine taking place on the same evening, with Man City’s English rivals Arsenal among those also in action at home to Borussia Dortmund.

This Champions League match will take place at Man City’s home the Etihad Stadium, which now holds a capacity of 61,470 spectators following a recent expansion.

Man City have lost only two of their last 27 home fixtures in the group stage/League Phase of the Champions League (W22 D3), though one of those was earlier this season against holders Paris Saint-Germain (4-2).

Man City vs. Napoli will be shown live on TNT Sports 1 or TNT Sports Ultimate for viewers in the UK.

Fans with the TNT Sports package through their TV provider can watch this game on Sky Go and Virgin TV Go, while this fixture will also be streamed live on Amazon Prime Video in the UK, and on CBS on Paramount+ in the USA.

Match highlights of Man City vs. Napoli will be available on Amazon Prime Video, TNT Sports and via BBC Sport’s dedicated UEFA Champions League Match of the Day show which you can watch live or stream on BBC iPlayer.

You can also view this match on the TNT Sports YouTube channel and both clubs' official YouTube accounts.

At the halfway stage in the League Phase, Man City sit seventh in the 36-team standings after accumulating nine points from their opening four matches.

Enzo Maresca’s side will realistically need at least a couple more victories to ensure they finish inside the top eight and secure automatic qualification for the last 16, rather than slip into the playoffs.

The Citizens have won each of their last three Champions League meetings with Napoli, most recently winning 2-0 on home soil in the League Phase of last season’s competition courtesy of goals from Erling Haaland and Jeremy Doku.

Napoli will therefore be out for revenge when they make the trip back to the blue side of Manchester, while Wednesday’s fixture also marks the return of City legend Kevin De Bruyne, whose first comeback to the Etihad was cut short.

Indeed, he was the unfortunate one sacrificed after just 21 minutes following a red card for Giovanni Di Lorenzo in Napoli's 2-0 defeat last season.

The Italian club have won one and lost three of their opening four UCL games this term, suffering a disappointing 4-1 defeat at Porto on November 4, and currently sit down in 27th place in the table, six points behind the top eight.

While Napoli enter this contest on the back of a narrow 1-0 home win over Torino in Serie A on Saturday, courtesy of a Scott McTominay goal, Man City were held to a frustrating 1-1 draw by Fulham in the Premier League.

#1988. Kepa handed Arsenal opportunity to prove he can fill Raya’s boots against Dortmund

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

With David Raya out, Kepa Arrizabalaga has a great chance to prove that he is more than just an Arsenal cup keeper. Mikel Arteta needs to have confidence in his number two. He needs to ensure that he upholds the same high bar set by the starting keeper as Borussia Dortmund come to the Emirates.

Raya has been ruled out of tonight’s Champions League game following a shoulder problem which he picked up in Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle United.

Whilst the initial diagnosis is good news, surgery is not required. Further tests will determine Raya’s recovery period.

As previously mentioned, Kepa will be stepping in for Raya at St James’ Park. Moreover, Arteta has stated his preferred choice of player in this situation. It seems that Illan Meslier will miss out on the opportunity to play this time.

As well as playing for Arsenal, the Spaniard has formerly played in the Champions League for Chelsea and Real Madrid. He has already appeared 14 times for the Gunners. Including in the league stage match which saw them beat Kairat Almaty.

Whilst Kepa has typically been second choice to Raya, his game time has mostly been in the EFL Cup. He will now need to prove himself as a trustworthy option for Arsenal should Raya be injured or otherwise unable to play.

As well as being a good goalkeeper, Raya is also good at passing and positioning. This in turn assists Arsenal in attacking from the back line.

Ex-Arsenal midfielder Paul Merson has acknowledged the quality that Spanish goalkeepers have at creating good defensive and central positioning. This can frequently be an under-recognised yet important component in Arsenal’s build-up play.

Like Arsenal, Kepa will also have to remain calm when playing out from the back. Although Kepa does not necessarily need to replicate all of Raya’s qualities, he will need to have good decision-making skills as well as good communication.

Meslier is still in contention, having played in the Carabao Cup game against Fleetwood Town. Kepa has been Arsenal’s number two keeper in the Premier League and was able to rush on in for Raya when he was substituted at Newcastle.

It does seem that Kepa is the obvious option, and he can further cement his position in Arteta’s team.

Arsenal’s schedule is demanding. They are playing Manchester City on a Sunday and there are also worries about Raya’s fitness. So far, the club has not yet received medical information on Raya’s status.

Then there is Dortmund. They have already secured victories in their first four games in the Champions League and are level on points with Arsenal in the league section.

Kepa does not have a great deal of flexibility. Arsenal require the new goalkeeper to offer them security.

In case Raya needs more time to recover, it is necessary for Arteta to be able to guarantee that there is an effective replacement.

For Kepa, it is equally an opportunity to prove that he can assume this leadership position for the team during important moments.

#1987. One selection choice boosts January transfer fund by millions | West Ham News

Switching several key players after the international break was a brave move designed to revitalise West Ham’s fortunes. Had the ball not crashed against the woodwork four times but nestled in the corner just once we’d all be proclaiming his changes as astute: Bringing back Alvarez and switching Morato to a centre back role weren’t rocket science but shored up a hitherto leaky defence.

However, bringing Fin Herrick into the side – ostensibly ‘resting’ (a.k.a.’dropping’) Hermansen – paid off . With Herrick now tried and tested, his elevation to credible first team keeper surely puts paid to any interest West Ham were showing in young Swansea ‘keeper Joe Duncan.

Herrick’s emergence means the budget doesn’t have to be diluted: Koppen can call off the search for a ‘keeper and find a goal scorer instead.

As Matt’s Claret and Hugh article last week predicted: “West Ham Could Save Themselves A Transfer Fee” by promoting Herrick rather than forking out millions to bring another promising young goal keeper to West Ham – when there’s one in situ already.

Exactly as it has seemed to pan out. Whilst Parker claims Hermansen has been strategically withdrawn for ‘some air’, there’s every chance that Herrick will get more match time whilst Areola remains unfit. And good luck to him. As he proved yesterday he’s got what it takes to keep a modest attack at bay.

A sterner test will come at Portsmouth but saving Koppen’s transfer budget for the acquisition of a striker who can actually hit the target looks to be the 100% absolute stone-cold priority in January, if it isn’t already too late.

And Herrick’s emergence has probably boosted the funds available to Koppen significantly.

In Episode 19 of The Mag Pod, we find Jamie, Simon, and Hutch reflecting on Newcastle United matches they have individually missed. Listen to the latest episode of The Mag Pod! Join Jamie, Simon, and Hutch for unfiltered football debate.

Jamie Smith missed Newcastle United’s 2–2 draw with Arsenal for a day out with old friends, so he’s asked Simon Cahill and Hutch to tell him what he missed at St James’ Park.

That turns out to include a second half Hutch reckons was Newcastle’s best of the season and a frosty reception for former captain Bruno Guimarães. It also leaves Jamie with a question for the other two. Which match do you still wish you’d been at?

First, Simon and Hutch try to account for the difference between the side that barely laid a glove on Arsenal before the break and the one that went 2–1 up. Simon picks out what changed down the right when Tino Livramento and Anthony Elanga got together. There’s also a second look at Arsenal’s equaliser and a difference of opinion over what VAR contributed to the afternoon.

The lads can understand wanting to give an Arsenal player a hard time while he’s on the ball. Where it gets more complicated is what happens after the final whistle.

Does the manner of Bruno’s departure change where he stands in Newcastle’s history?

And is it fair to put him in the same bracket as Alexander Isak?

Jamie’s article for The Mag, Missing Home Matches, brings back memories of a 4–3 comeback against Norwich just days after his son was born.

Simon remembers catching Moussa Sissoko’s afternoon against Chelsea on a tiny telly in a Northumberland pub.

Hutch explains why he watched Newcastle beat Sunderland 3–0 alongside his daughter despite having a ticket for the away end.

Finally, Jamie and Hutch look ahead to their first visit to the Amex, with chips and ice cream on Brighton seafront promised whatever the weather.

#1984. Can Ethan Nwaneri play against Arsenal for Borussia Dortmund in Champions League?

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 09:36

Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri will reunite with his parent club when Borussia Dortmund take on the Premier League champions in Tuesday's Champions League clash at the Emirates Stadium.

The 19-year-old joined the German giants on a season-long loan during the final hours of the summer transfer window, but he is yet to find his best form under Niko Kovac.

Nwaneri has only provided one assist and no goals from his first 13 appearances in a Dortmund shirt across all competitions, that contribution coming on his Bundesliga debut against Hoffenheim.

Since then, the 2007-born playmaker has only started four Bundesliga matches, and he is still waiting to make a first XI in the Champions League, being restricted to 87 minutes across four substitute outings.

Nwaneri was also given just a one-minute run-out in the weekend's 1-0 Bundesliga win over Borussia Monchengladbach, but he may be given the chance to strut his stuff against his boyhood team.

Champions League rules permit loan players to face their parent clubs in the Champions League, so Nwaneri will be able to feature in Arsenal vs. Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night.

Unlike in the Premier League and other domestic competitions in England, where loan players cannot take on parent teams without special dispensation, there are no such restrictions outlined in the Champions League rules and regulations.

However, if Nwaneri was to return to Arsenal in January, the England Under-21 international would not be able to feature for the Premier League champions for the remainder of the tournament.

Article 30.05 of UEFA's Champions League regulations states that 'A player may not play in the UEFA Champions League, UEFA Europa League or UEFA Conference League for more than one club in a single season', but Arsenal are not expected to bring Nwaneri back to North London over the winter.

The teenager has scored 10 goals and set up two more in 51 Arsenal games since making his debut against Brentford in September 2022, when he became the Premier League's youngest player of all time.

Goal Bayern Munich. Philippe Coutinho. 2-8.

Loan players making decisive contributions against parent clubs in the Champions League has been a semi-regular occurrence, the most notable example being Philippe Coutinho in 2020.

The then-Barcelona playmaker was shipped out to Bayern Munich and reunited with La Blaugrana in the quarter-finals of the 2019-20 edition, when he incredibly scored twice in an 8-2 annihilation.

Sixteen years prior, Fernando Morientes - on loan at Monaco from Real Madrid - scored in both legs of the quarter-final against Los Blancos, helping Les Monegasques knock out his parent team on away goals before they lost to Porto in the final.

Real were also stung by James Rodriguez in the 2017-18 semi-finals vs. Bayern Munich, but the Colombian's goal - which he refused to celebrate - was not enough to prevent Los Blancos advancing 4-3 on aggregate.

The 2013-14 semi-finals saw Thibaut Courtois play a crucial role in Atletico Madrid's success against parent club Chelsea, who tried to force Los Rojiblancos to pay them £2.5m for each game the Belgian goalkeeper played against them, only for UEFA to rule the terms null, void and unenforceable.

#1983. Reports: Milan watching on as Man Utd confirm renewal talks with Fernandes

Bruno Fernandes has ended up on AC Milan’s radar ahead of the summer, according to reports, with a free transfer potentially on the cards.

Ever since the summer, when the BBC were the first to report on Milan’s interest, Fernandes has been brought up by various outlets as an option for the Rossoneri. Just a few days ago, Fabrizio Romano said he is ‘more than a dream’ for them and that Ruben Amorim could be key.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Having just turned 32, Fernandes is still at a good age and he’s showing that with Manchester United so far this season. In 14 appearances, he has bagged six goals and three assists, so it’s no surprise that many clubs are monitoring his situation given the expiring contract.

As reported by both Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews) and Tuttosport (via MilanNews) this morning, Milan are seriously evaluating the idea of signing him. It’s still too early to talk about negotiations, but he’s definitely on their radar and will likely remain there.

Of course, if he does end up leaving on a free transfer, there will be no shortage of suitors so Milan would likely have to table a hefty contract offer. The club owner, Gerry Cardinale, seems more willing to do that now, though, than he did just a year ago.

One potential problem is that Manchester United have confirmed that they are discussing a renewal with the player. The CEO Omar Berrada showered the Portuguese star with praise, as cited by Fabrizio Romano, so it seems a stay in Manchester cannot be ruled out either.

#1982. Stupidity or loyalty? Pat Nevin poses key Newcastle United question

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

This follows Saturday’s game against Arsenal.

Plenty of angles to look at and debate from a very eventful 90+ minutes.

Plus of course all of the subplots that swirled around this Newcastle United v Arsenal fixture.

Pat Nevin sees a lot of Newcastle United, the former Chelsea and Everton winger a regular visitor at St James’ Park.

He was on media duties this weekend as well.

Reflecting back on his latest visit, Pat Nevin detailing in the Football Extra newsletter: “I nipped down to a freezing St James’ Park at the weekend, where the reception for their beloved former midfielder Bruno Guimaraes made the weather feel positively balmy. Hell hath no fury like a Geordie scorned, but fortunately the home side played so well in the second half that, at one stage, they forgot to boo him for a good two whole minutes.”

Pat Nevin adding: “I understand why football fans feel this way. Having lost Antony Gordon, Alexander Isak and Sandro Tonali already, it was a heavy blow to lose the one who mirrored their passions the most. Players think differently. The idea of turning down the English champions, who could win the Champions League, and instead stay at a club that is shipping out all of the best talent around you, is demanding an unthinkable level of loyalty. Most would substitute loyalty for stupidity in that sentence.”

I suppose that also sums up my many decades of following Newcastle United, especially when non-football fans ask me why I do it…

Back to Saturday’s match though and Pat Nevin: “Arsenal were fabulous and the gulf between the teams looked enormous in the first half but the comeback after the break could well be my favourite 45 minutes of the season so far. From nowhere, Newcastle bullied, dominated, outran and even outplayed Arsenal. It was glorious stuff. Now comes the tough part as manager Matthias Jaissle has to recreate that feeling every week.”

As Newcastle United fans,, what will our stupidity/loyalty be rewarded with in the weeks and months to come?

At the same time, a gutsy point at Brighton followed by home wins over Man U and the Mackems, then the world will feel a very different place.

#1981. Watford vs Blackburn Rovers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 09:53

Watford play host to Blackburn Rovers on Wednesday night searching for yet another permanent head coach after the sacking of Alessio Dionisi.

At a time when the Hornets sit in 21st position in the Championship table, Rovers make the trip to Vicarage Road sitting among the mid-table places.

Whenever a new manager arrives at Watford, there is always an inevitability that his stay at Vicarage Road will be a short one.

A 10th defeat across 18 matches in all competitions led to Dionisi being dismissed after Saturday's 4-0 defeat at Sheffield United.

With Watford having earned four points from games against Lincoln City and Middlesbrough before the international break, it feels that the Italian could have been provided with more time in the dugout.

Instead, the Pozzo Family has decided to act with Watford ending the weekend sitting four points above the relegation zone.

On a positive note, Watford are unbeaten in their last three games at Vicarage Road, collecting seven points in the process, while they have only conceded nine goals in eight home league fixtures during 2026-27.

As for Blackburn, they responded to Tony Mowbray stepping down from his first-team duties with a 2-2 draw at rivals Burnley on Sunday.

Having twice come from behind, Rovers will be satisfied with a deserved share of the spoils at Turf Moor, a result that keeps them 11 points above the relegation zone despite being viewed as one of the favourites for the drop in the summer.

Furthermore, 17 points have been accumulated from their last 10 games, emphasising that they could still challenge for a top-eight spot this campaign.

However, Blackburn remain with just one away win this campaign, only recording seven points from eight matches while shipping 15 goals.

While the Watford lineup and formation is difficult to predict, personnel changes are expected after the drab performance at Sheffield United.

Hector Kyprianou, Rocco Vata and Luca Kjerrumgaard are all options in midfield and attack.

Three Watford players - Mattie Pollock, Kevin Keben and Martin Payero - are all one yellow card away from a one-match ban.

With Tom Atcheson expected to miss out with the head injury that he sustained at Burnley, Blackburn could switch to a back four.

Jayden Fevrier was introduced as an early substitute at Turf Moor before he was replaced by Ryoya Morishita 62 minutes later, so the latter could get the nod here.

Second-choice goalkeeper Aynsley Pears will remain between the sticks, a consequence of Balasz Toth being ruled out until January with a hand injury.

Ravaglia; Traore, Coulibaly, Pollock, Keben, Bola; Kayembe, Kyprianou; Vata, Kjerrumgaard, Mavididi

Blackburn Rovers possible starting lineup:

Pears; Beyuku, McLoughlin, Carter, Pickering; Montgomery, Baradji; Morishita, Cantwell, Afolayan; Gudjohnsen

Although both of these teams are without a permanent manager in charge, Blackburn are far more settled than Watford. With that in mind, we are backing the visitors to earn a deserved victory at Vicarage Road, keeping themselves within touching distance of the playoffs in the process.

#1980. West Ham’s striker woes put into sharp relief after yet another goal

Scott Parker’s decision to recall Soungoutou Magassa from the ‘Nuno wilderness’ back into the West Ham fold looks well founded.

Similarly, the apparent re-integration of Edson Alvarez into West Ham United’s starting eleven last weekend has been met with almost universal approval after the Mexican’s decent showing against Preston.

At the very least, these two players will see their transfer values rise simply by being deployed in competitive football. At best, they could contribute significantly towards a successful outcome for the club this season.

All of which makes Niclas Fullkrug’s escapades in Germany even more ironic, as West Ham’s failure to score their winner after thirty attempts gets put into sharp relief by their on-loan striker becoming the Bundesliga’s top scorer.

Another goal by Fullkrug at the weekend in Bremen’s 4- 0 victory will make Hammers fans scratch their head and wonder whether, with different coaching and different attitudes, the German could have made an impact in east London this season. He’d certainly have got some game time.

Fullkrug is now the top scorer in the German league after his ninth goal for Werder Bremen at the weekend

Too late to think about recalling Fullkrug, it seems he’s found his spiritual ‘home’, and good luck to him.

It does throw the coaching failures of the last three of West Ham’s so called ‘managers’ sharply into focus when they all relied heavily on their favourites and ‘fell out’ frequently with players: Who can forget Lopetegui’s dressing room bust-ups with Mohammed Kudus and Jean-Clair Todibo?

Eye-watering sums are spent by football clubs on researching, scouting and recruiting players, but then whole careers seem ended on a managerial whim or a clash of egos.

By no means unique to West Ham, but it is an area in which clubs have to learn to do better or risk losing, as in Fullkrug’s case, the very stars who can fire the goals they’ve just paid through the nose to acquire.

‘ We handed them the momentum and when the crowd there gets up for it you’re in a bit of trouble.’

‘Seen poor Newcastle teams take points off prime Man United, chelsea and liverpool teams. Once the crowd and players start believing its always going to be a tough fixture.’

‘Newcastle were fantastic for 20/25 minutes in the second half.’

‘Newcastle scammed a draw here and should be thanking their lucky stars.’

‘Treatment of MLS is again a sackable offense, bench Bruno.’

‘Not much to complain about tbh. We actually scored two beauties but made some very un-Arsenal like errors.’

‘All the teams have so much quality. Just a little drop in performance and you gonna suffer.

‘Our xG for the match was between 1.4-1.5, which was mostly created in the first half, but its not enough given how dominant we were.

We didnt really miss any clear chances in that first half.

We just keep on exepcting to exceed our xG like we have so far this season.’

‘Newcastle only needed one chance to change the game in thier way.’

‘The two individual errors for their goals lost us the points here. Both teams had chances to score more goals, so a draw is probably the right result.’

‘Suddenly Newcastle + the crowd are up for it. For the next 20 or so minutes we abandoned our principles and collapsed.’

‘Just realised for Newcastle 2nd. Timber is marking Dan Burn, Dan Burn makes a run to to some space, Timber follows but a Newcastle player grabs Timber meaning Burn is free. Quite clever tbf.’

‘Problem has not and will not change. When teams want to get something out of the match, they will press every player 1v1, except Madueke and Eze. The rest of our players then panic. Same recipe, every match.

Newcastle waited until the second half to do this to make it difficult for Arteta to adjust.

Eze at 10 MLS at 8 Madueke wide right Then find a baller or speed demon on the left and we will the league by 15 point.

Until then, 1 goal wins or draws. Get comfortable with it.’

‘If it were that easy how were we 9-0-1 coming into this match? What a really odd tactic for Newcastle, get absolutely battered in the first half and then hatch their plan.’

‘That they waited until the second half to man to man press us is just not true. Like not even something that can be argued, just factually wrong. ‘Couldn’t watch the game, but it seems like a decent point in hindsight, especially at a bit of a bogey ground.’

‘Drawing away at a difficult ground is decent enough.’

‘They actually pressed all game. We were just better at creating the situations out of it in the first half. They simply went a bit more aggressive on certain players (man to man) and then the mistakes crept into our game.’

‘Nah they definitely didn’t do high press or pressed with intensity in the first half. It’s more of half press and then fall back to position.

Even in the 2nd half, without Ode’s error I don’t think they can get back in the game. Momentum + crowd backing is a strange thing in football.

Newcastle is a very average team this year, and super young. It’s definitely 2 points drop because of us, not their quality nor Jaissle tactics.’

‘Error from Ødegaard is the clear catalyst for Newcastle to get back into the match. They made triple sub at HT but we conceded barely 3-4 minutes after the restart. Without that error, I don’t think Newcastle score, I think they definitely would have improved though.’

‘Football is a low scoring game. I can excuse one mistake leading to a goal vs an opponent thats 3+ levels below ours. I can excuse a bit of panic as they throw everything at us. I can’t excuse 2 goals in 20 minutes of absolute domination where we’re playing like a league 2 team versus a team that was already playing like a league 2 team. I can’t excuse not putting 2+ versus a team that lies down in front of you the way they did in the first half.’

#1978. Report highlights Nuno’s treatment of ‘frozen out’ West Ham players

Mexican Edson Alvarez has received plaudits after his satisfactory return to the West Ham United starting line up following Scott Parker’s decision to re-integrate him into the side. Alvarez’ evident emotional release at being recalled to the team is testimony to the struggle he’s endured both on, and off the pitch since last playing a league game as a West Ham player.

Injury, surgery, kidnapping scandal, covid certificate allegations – all must have taken their toll on the Alvarez family as did Nuno’s decision to freeze the midfielder out of the West Ham team after, it must be said, a pretty decent World Cup.

Here is a player who had not started a competitive fixture since August yet he was ready to go when called upon and lasted a whole 90 minutes. As reported by futnsoccer.com, Nuno’s treatment of the Mexican national team captain evidently took a big toll, and it was only through his own resilience that he was able to jump when Scott Parker called:

“It has been a very difficult period for me after four months without playing, you know? And a lot of things happening in my life, a lot of changes,” Alvarez said.

“Imagine being away from the team, like training alone…..I’ve been working really hard by myself, and I’m just looking forward”.

Emotional and successful return for Edson Alvarez: Who’d have thought it.

Alvarez was so moved that he sought Parker out before the start of the game:

“I spoke with [Parker] at the beginning of the game and I said thank you. I said thank you to him because he is giving me again the opportunity, the chance to show myself, and that means a lot to me.”

“I need to pay him back that confidence, and I think the only way that I can do it is on the pitch; like showing myself, fighting, and doing everything with my experience for the team. I really missed it.”

In a team famously devoid of leadership, it sounds as if Scott Parker has just found himself a lieutenant who will go into battle for him – and for West Ham – any time he’s asked. All of which can only throw into question Nuno’s decision to ‘exile’ Alvarez and so many other players from the training ground.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

Wonder what it takes for a manager to have his UEFA Pro license revoked pending investigation of unprofessional and detrimental conduct. Perhaps with DK & Koppen, we can draw a line beneath it all. Whatever SP achieves or not, he is not a paranoid megalomaniac who thinks he is God’s gift.

He’s out of the Marmite pot you either love him or hate him. This is shown by the contradictory opinions of the fans. Continually spoken about leadership on the field when Rice left he was one person suggested as captain. Other two are Veltman and Soucek but they may not play 90 minutes. Nuno carried a big chip on his shoulder for a number of players. Nobody can deny he is OTT sometimes but this is his nature.

He’ll probably get a straight red next game. Let’s hold our houses on the praise. Lost count of how many balls he kicked straight out of touch.

It’s a really big plus if a motivated in form Alvarez is in the team. We have missed a serious defensive midfielder. Just need a similar centre forward who actually scores and we could be a transformed team.

What an education for Magassa as well, seeing and sometimes replacing a Mexican international of some note

Alvarez is exactly the type of player we will need to drag us back up the table. I’d like him to engage less with the referee, because that usually only ends up one way, but other than that he’s an excellent asset.

Great point about engaging with the referee, Alan.

It will have been a long, long time since Edson Alvarez was involved in games at Championship level. Just like everyone else, he will need to learn very quickly that there are no reviews and we need to get on with it without the confrontation, protest or the waiting for support and sympathy.

Alvarez did the team talk immediately before kick off. While the attitude of the likes of Todibo were always questionable that did not seem to be the case with Alvarez. Alvarez is fiery but that should be manageable surely, it’s part of why managers are called managers they’re supposed to be able to manage.

#1976. Di Marzio: Milan among Italian clubs looking to bolster academy with Malmö FF talent

AC Milan are thinking about bolstering their academy with the Malmö FF talent Leon Da Silva, according to a report.

In recent months, a lot of focus has been on how Milan will reinforce the first team in January and next summer. Understandably so, as Gerry Cardinale seemingly has big spending plans, keen on making it back to the Champions League next season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Amidst all of the first-team rumours, however, Milan are also working on the academy. Jovan Kirovski is evaluating players for the Futuro side with his team, while Vincenzo Vergine (pictured) and his team are doing so for the Primavera and below.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio, one of the players on Milan’s wish list is Leon Da Silva, who currently plays in the academy of Malmö FF. At the age of 16, he’s yet to make his debut with the first team, but he did feature in a friendly game last month.

Da Silva plays as a centre-back and as the report states, he has even been compared to Virgil Van Dijk for how he plays. Since he’s still very young, if Milan were to secure his services, he would start with the Primavera team (or even in the younger sides).

In addition to Milan, the likes of Inter and Torino are also monitoring the Swede, though it seems Malmö are keen on keeping him for a few more years.

#1975. You’ll not believe these incredible West Ham stats that defy all explanation

Football is often described as a results business, but every now and then the underlying statistics tell a completely different story to the league table. Right now, West Ham United are providing one of the most puzzling examples of that phenomenon.

Using BBC Sports match stats data, over our last five matches, the Hammers have registered an astonishing 111 shots, with 35 of those efforts hitting the target.

Those are numbers you would normally associate with a Championship elite attacking side. To put it into perspective, averaging more than 22 shots per game and seven on target suggests a team consistently creating chances, putting opponents under pressure and spending large periods on the front foot.

All too familiar expression of Hermansen anguish

During the same five-game period, West Ham have conceded just 19 shots on target. That points to a side that is not only attacking effectively but also controlling matches overall defensively yet there have still been some major lapses in defence, which has led to conceding “sloppy” goals – 12 in total!

So despite posting overall metrics that would not look out of place among title challengers, West Ham have failed to win any of those five games!

Having watched four of those five matches, the answer seems fairly clear, goalkeeping and costly mistakes at the back have been the biggest contributing factors. While only scoring 8 goals from those 35 shots on target suggests major improvements up front is required!

Against Preston, Herrick was required to make just one save but still conceded, despite the visitors registering only two shots on target. Piroe contributed largely towards their goal.

Compare that with Mads Hermansen’s recent run.

At Ewood Park, Blackburn managed just three shots on target but scored twice, with only one effort being saved.

Cardiff recorded four shots on target and found the net three times, with Hermansen making a single save.

It gets worse when West Bromwich Albion visited the London stadium and had three shots on target, they scored with all three, and Hermansen was unable to make a save.

Southampton generated seven shots on target and scored three goals. On that occasion, Hermansen acquitted himself better, making four saves, but the pattern remains clear, opponents have been converting a remarkably high proportion of their chances.

The data suggests a team that should be winning far more matches than it is.

What’s going on at West Ham? How can a team produce 111 shots, 35 on target, concede only 19 shots on target, and still fail to win a single game in five matches?

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

Not wishing to nit-pick the stats, but I’m pretty sure Herrick made a double save in the first half, that’s 2 saves? Having watched all 5 games, West Ham have been unfortunate in all 5 them in different ways.

Because we start games incredibly poorly but then go on to dominate most opponents for the rest of the game. We are like Jekyl and Hyde in the same game, game after game.

This team is a sleeping giant and it feels like it’s starting to wake (hurry up!). Makes you feel sorry for the rest of the division when it does, and that better be soon.

Harsh on Mads, I feel. I don’t think that there was much any ‘keeper could have done better to keep out the Cardiff City goals.

It is the unity and cohesion of the whole team that is the best defence. The figures don’t lie, obviously, but sometimes circumstances or opposition good fortune get in the way of the results these figures suggest.

Perseverance and faith will turn the tide. Good fortune will prevail in the end. What will be, will be. All that is needed is the daily effort and enjoying the gradual progress.

Harsh on Mads? He may genuinely be the worst keeper i’ve seen in Claret and Blue. He get’s absolutely nowhere near anything and a shot on target is pretty much a goal. Herrick doesn’t look like the answer but it was definitely an improvement. I’m hoping Areola is back sooner rather than later.

#1974. Stoke City vs Millwall - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 10:10, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 12:53

Stoke City square off against Millwall on Wednesday night looking for the win that would keep the club in the automatic promotion spots of the Championship table.

At a time when the Potters are in second position, Alex Neil returns to one of his former clubs, with the Lions beginning the week in 16th place.

The November international break came at the wrong time for Stoke, who have established themselves as contenders for promotion to the Premier League.

Nevertheless, Mark Robins's side returned on Saturday with a 1-0 win over then-leaders Birmingham City, making it 10 victories from their last 13 games in the Championship.

Rather incredibly, Stoke have accumulated 16 points from their last six games without scoring more than twice in a single match.

Just two goals have been conceded during that period, while Stoke have four clean sheets from their most recent six games at the bet365 Stadium, including their last three.

Despite starting the campaign with three successive defeats, no team in the Championship has won more games (10) than Stoke in 2026-27.

Meanwhile, Neil returns to the bet365 Stadium with Millwall having lost five of their most recent seven games.

Three successive defeats, the latest a 1-0 home loss to Queens Park Rangers after Zak Sturge was sent off in the 15th minute, have left the Scot fighting to keep his job at The Den.

Millwall, who reached the playoffs last season, are nine points adrift of eighth spot, and defeat to Stoke would leave the East London outfit cut adrift from the mid-table places.

As well as losing five of their eight away matches this campaign, Millwall have conceded 18 goals on their travels, the joint-second worst defensive record in such fixtures in the division.

Stoke could make at least three changes, a consequence of Luca Bombino's red card against Birmingham and Djibril Soumare and George Hirst both picking up injuries in the same game.

Eric-Junior Bocat should start at left wing-back, Svante Ingelsson is in line to feature in midfield should Ethan Galbraith not return after illness, and Sam Gallagher could get the nod ahead of Robert Bozenik in attack.

Million Manhoef may also start on one of the flanks should Robins wish to introduce further fresh legs.

Meanwhile, Alfie Doughty could be introduced as a straight replacement for suspended Millwall defender Zak Sturge.

With the Lions having failed to score in three successive matches, Zak Lovelace and Mihailo Ivanovic will feel they are in contention to start in the final third.

Luke Cundle, Romain Esse and Josh Coburn will all be assessed after missing the QPR defeat on Saturday.

Johansson; Wilmot, Lawal, Graham; Johnson, Ingelsson, McGlynn, Bocat; Devenny, Gallagher, Bae

Jensen; Sykes, Taylor, Cooper, Doughty; De Norre, Metcalfe; Neghli, Arconte, Lovelace; Ivanovic

While this contest could prove to be closer than many are anticipating, it is difficult to back against a Stoke side that have kept clean sheets in their last three home games, especially against a Millwall team that have conceded 18 goals on the road and are without the suspended Zak Sturge. With that in mind, we are predicting a narrow win for the Potters.

#1973. A disappointing end to a disappointing match for Newcastle United Women

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Coming into the Newcastle United Women game with Nottingham Forest, both sides knew they were already eliminated from the Subway Players cup, so it was perhaps always going to be something of a ‘Dead Rubber’.

But with an international break looming it was still a chance for some players to stake a claim for a starting berth when the action resumes.

Forest made a raft of changes with Grace McEwen and Ebba Hed joining the ever-present Hannah Coan in central defence, with the trio forming a near impenetrable barrier. Both Codie Thomas and the rapid Deanne Rose operated on the flanks to great effect and caused United problems throughout.

They went with a midfield three of Rachel Rowe sitting in front of the impressive and hard working pair Georgia Brougham and Tove Almsqvist. While Norwegian Tuva Espas and the on loan Lois Shooter partnered one another up front and looked lively.

Newcastle United Women made some subtle changes with Kayla Rendell coming back in goal, while Jemma Purfield returned to the back four. Mollie Lambert was given a chance to play in her favoured central midfield berth while Beth Lumsden shifted over to the left wing to accommodate Leanne Kiernan, who was starting against her former side.

Newcastle enjoyed the majority of the possession but clear cut chances were few and far between, with any opportunities that were created seemed to be snatched at or fired over the bar.

The Lady Mags created a couple of opportunities early on, with Beth Lumsden and Lois Joel going close. Before Jordan Nobbs was denied by the impressive Hannah Coan inside the area with a crucial block. Nobbs had another chance soon after, but her effort from a tight angle out wide was claimed by Forest goalie Georgie Ferguson.

Forest were creating chances of their own though. Codie Thomas put the ball into the box from the left, but Tuva Espas was unable to steer her header on target. However, they were soon ahead and with it the game changed over a four minute passage of play.

A speculative cross from Canadian international Deanne Rose out on the left was aimed at picking out Tove Almqvist but it flashed across goal and looked to be ushered out by Kayla Rendell. The goalie, on-loan from Manchester United, let the ball go past her as she assumed it was going wide of her far post, only to look foolish when the ball actually crept in off the woodwork.

Despite that setback Newcastle United Women responded well and from the ensuing kick-off were almost back level. Beth Lumsden playing on her less favoured left flank sent in a deep cross which was headed wide by Lambert.

But moments later Forest doubled their lead, when Tuva Espas forced a turnover in the United half and, spotting Rendell off her line, lobbed a perfect shot over the stranded goalie and into the net from 40 yards out.

Forest could have been three goals to the good before the break as Rachel Rowe worked the ball into the box, but was unable to find the final pass.

Newcastle had a lot of work to do in the second half but it was Forest who were looking the more dangerous side. Tove Almqvist played a ball over the Lasses defence as she tried to pick out Espas in the box, but Rendell was just able to gather it first.

It perhaps should have been 3-0 to the East Midlands side when a brilliant move was started by captain Georgia Brougham. She played the ball into Rowe who in turn found Espas, with the Norwegian international able to advance down the right before sending a great ball in for her strike partner Lois Shooter. However, United captain Rachel McLauchlan got there first and sent her clearance onto the post and very nearly into her own net before it bounced clear to safety.

Forest continued to create chances after that. Rowe curled an effort from the edge of the area and Rose continued to be a nuisance on the wing as she carried the ball with confidence into the final third and won a free-kick. Then did excellently to keep hold of the ball before playing it into the centre circle, to substitute Aimee Claypole, but she sent her effort straight at Rendell.

Claypole, who was on loan at Durham a couple of seasons ago, missed another chance after Freya Thomas played the ball into her feet. Her effort took a deflection before being collected once again by Rendell. Rose had another chance in stoppage time but could only find the side netting.

There were very few clear cut chances in the remainder of the game with Jordan Nobbs perhaps going closest when forcing Ferguson into a low save. Codie Thomas was also strong defensively and prevented another Newcastle shot. While Purfield fired over the bar from close range before sending a corner into Ferguson’s hands.

On what was a frustrating day for Newcastle, one bright spark was the introduction of Jessie Gale who ran her socks off after coming on, putting the Forest backline under rare pressure. The youngster’s cross/shot forced Ferguson into a save to preserve her clean sheet.

With just seconds left of stoppage time frustration began to tell and when Lois Joel shot into the net after the referee blew his whistle she was shown a yellow card, which then turned to red for dissent.

A disappointing end to what was a disappointing day.

Newcastle United: Kayla Rendell, Rachel McLauchlan (c), Hanna Németh (Aoife Mannion 88), Jemma Purfield, Kaitlyn Torpey, Lois Joel, Mollie Lambert (Jessie Gale 54), Jordan Nobbs, Beth Lumsden (Emilia Larsson 67), Martha Thomas, Leanne Kiernan (Kathleen McGovern 54).

Subs not used: Anna Tamminen, Hildur Antonsdóttir, Oona Sevenius, Gemma Evans, Abbie Richardson.

Nottingham Forest: Georgie Ferguson, Codie Thomas, Grace McEwen, Hannah Coan, Ebba Hed (Abbie Lafayette 89), Deanne Rose, Georgia Brougham (Freya Thomas 72), Tove Almqvist (Cerys Brown 89), Rachel Rowe, Tuva Espas (Aimee Claypole 62), Lois Shooter (Shania Hayles 61).

Subs not used: Katie Cox, Lucy Carney, Melissa Johnson, Lily Stevenson.

The League Cup has adopted a Swiss League format for fixtures, with only the top eight teams of 23 progressing to the quarter finals. Both Newcastle and Forest were already mathematically eliminated before this game so the result matters very little.

If you ignore the games played against WSL 1 sides Aston Villa and Everton, then Newcastle have conceded five goals in all competitions this season with four of those coming against Forest, who like United are still unbeaten in the league. That suggests the Lace City side should be one to look out for in the second half of the season, as along with Sunderland, they are the best side to face the Lady Mags so far.

A final concern was the standard of officiating for this game. With this being a clash between two second tier sides and a premier competition, surely the standard of the referee and assistants should be better than using ones from the local Non-League circuit. There are plenty of top female officials in the top tiers of the women’s game so surely both Newcastle and Forest deserved better? A referee who needlessly sent off a player in the 94th minute and his flag waving buddies who struggled to keep up with the play throughout the game, simply isn’t good enough.

Newcastle only have one WSL 2 game remaining before the Christmas break, against Watford on Sunday, 20th December.

There is now an international break before an FA Cup Third Round tie away to Manchester Unity on the 13th December with the host team based in Chadderton, Oldham. The Lasses faced the same opponents in the cup back in November 2023, winning 9-2 away from home on that occasion. But following the game both sets of fans developed a great likeness for one another with many Newcastle fans supporting Unity in their games over the past three years.

The following Wednesday sees Newcastle bring their League Cup campaign to a close with current leaders Manchester United set to visit St James’ Park for a rare midweek game under the floodlights.

With a trio of front men who are struggling to put the ball into the net, West Ham face an uphill battle to end their five game run without a win with a trip to Fratton Park tomorrow night.

Joel Piroe remains the best of a poor bunch of Hammers front men with four West Ham goals to his name – whilst Taty Castellanos and Pablo have a solitary strike each.

Matt’s article earlier highlighted the woeful statistics of shots per game and goals resulting – the Hammers simply have to do better. Reports suggest Castellanos will be on his way in January to accommodate a replacement.

Closer to home, West Ham already have one youngster who is making waves: Dan Cummings, just loaned out to Aldershot in the fifth tier, has already broken his duck with a strike on debut against Scunthorpe United. Scott Parker has already proven with Finn Herrick’s selection that he’s not afraid to select young talent where appropriate.

20 year-old Cummings had been on the pitch just a few minutes into his debut. According to West Ham’s own web site, he:

“Chased down a long ball on the right edge of the Scunthorpe penalty area before beating his defender, cutting inside and sliding the ball under goalkeeper Maison Campbell with his right foot.

The goal came just six minutes after Cummings had been introduced from the substitutes’ bench“.

If Cummings carries on in that vein he’ll soon be on Scott Parker’s radar: As a third or fourth striker option who is young, fast, enthusiastic, match fit and prepared to chase everything, what is the worst that could happen?

Hitting the target at the moment appears to be a very rare skill at West Ham United: A couple of months’ more with half a dozen goals and Cummings could well have the opportunity of making a name for himself in front of a significantly larger crowd than Aldershot’s 2,252.

#1970. Inter Milan's Francesco Pio Esposito branded "unstoppable" by Italian media as Man United consider move for striker "like [Erling] Haaland"

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 10:35, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 10:37

Francesco Pio Esposito was in sensational form on Sunday, scoring a hat-trick in Inter Milan's 4-4 draw with Atalanta BC in Serie A.

The 21-year-old has now netted seven times and registered two assists in 14 appearances for Inter during the 2026-27 campaign, and there is currently a host of speculation surrounding his future at San Siro.

Manchester United allegedly recently scouted the 6ft 3in striker, with the Red Devils planning to bring in a new forward next year.

Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur have also been linked with Esposito, who has 18 goals and nine assists in 64 appearances for Inter in all competitions.

As expected, the form of the Italy international against Atalanta drew huge praise from the Italian media.

What did the Italian media say about Esposito performance?

Corriere dello Sport handed Esposito an overall performance rating of 8/10 and branded the striker "unstoppable" for his excellent display.

Tuttosport called the striker "Super Pio" and focused on his contribution to Inter's attacking display, but it was still not enough to secure his side all three points.

Tuttomercatoweb said "Esposito like Haaland" during their post-match piece, with the Inter forward being compared to Manchester City and Norway striker Erling Haaland.

Meanwhile, Sky Sport Italia gave him Inter's highest rating of 8/10.

Benjamin Sesko's ongoing injury problems are expected to put Man United in the market for a new striker in January, but they might have to wait until the end of the campaign to bring in a big-name player in that area of the field.

Inter are said to value Esposito in the region of £84m, but that could prove to be a bargain if he continues to develop throughout the 2026-27 campaign.

Esposito has scored 10 times in 15 appearances for Italy, and he seemingly has the skill set to be a huge success in the Premier League.

Man United may bring in an experienced option, most likely on loan, during the January market, before launching a big-money move for Esposito next summer, providing that they are able to hold off the threat of Premier League relegation.

#1968. Champions League suspended players: Manchester United blow as quartet to miss this week's games

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 10:53

The league phase of the Champions League continues this week as the 36 teams head into matchday five looking for the win that could prove decisive in their quest to progress through to the knockout stages.

Arsenal's showdown with Borussia Dortmund is arguably the pick of the matches, with those teams sitting at the top of the Premier League and Bundesliga tables.

Nevertheless, with all of the favourites for the competition being kept apart on this particular matchday, they will view it as an opportunity to edge closer to making the top eight.

As for AEK Athens, Aboubakary Koita is unavailable for their match against Como due to the red card that he was given versus Real Madrid.

Koita was handed a red card after the final whistle for a prolonged confrontation with the officials.

Sabah defender Aden McCarthy is the fourth player to miss the MD5 for his dismissal in the 4-1 defeat to Viking FK.

He now misses the home fixture against La Liga champions Barcelona.

Although Koita and McCarthy will miss matches this week, UEFA are currently indicating that an extra game may be added to their suspensions in due course.

#1967. Stunning from Matthias Jaissle, this is excellent

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Matthias Jaissle didn’t have the smoothest of arrivals at Newcastle United.

Disgruntled at him choosing to move on and United meeting his £9.5m release clause, Al Ahli delaying paperwork so he couldn’t start work with NUFC until only 18 days before the Premier League season kicked off.

A Newcastle United team that had finished 12th last season in the Premier League under an impossible 58 game schedule across all competitions.

Coming in and inheriting a team that lost star players Tonali, Trippier, Gordon and Bruno this summer, then see a Sporting Director in control of a very defined focus on overwhelmingly recruiting younger players from overseas with the hope they will increase in quality and value across the coming years.

Fair to say this was always going to be a season of challenge for Matthias Jaissle.

Returning after the latest international break, the toughest possible matches awaited.

Reigning champions/current leaders Arsenal at St James’ Park, then away at Brighton, the only team to take any points off Arsenal in the opening ten rounds of Premier League matches.

Arsenal turned up on Saturday and did what they have done all season, they suffocated Newcastle United across the entire first half.

The Gunners passed and passed, The Magpies chased and chased.

Arsenal kept the ball, Newcastle couldn’t get it.

Matthias Jaissle’s team couldn’t get out of their own half and once the visitors took the lead, I would be surprised if any Newcastle United fan thought this would be anything other than a defeat.

In 14 Premier League and Champions League matches so far, Arsenal had won 12, lost that game at Brighton, plus drew 2-2 at Bayern Munich.

Apart from those Bayern and Brighton matches, Arsenal had conceded a grand total of three goals across the other 12 matches in the Champions League and Premier League, an average of a goal every 6+ hours in these dozen games.

Ahead of Saturday’s second half, Arsenal had Newcastle United right where they wanted them. Having dominated the opposition and taking the lead, if the home side came out and tried to get back into the game, gaps would open for the visitors to ruthlessly exploit. It is the Arsenal way.

The second half about to start and Matthias Jaissle surprises everybody, three subs at such an early stage. Jacob Ramsey, Anthony Elanga and Tino Livramento replacing Sean Steur, Jacob Murphy and Amar Dedic.

From the first whistle of that second period it was Newcastle United on the front foot. Going toe to toe with Arsenal, or rather, stamping on their toes.

It was exhilarating, it was what we love to see, what we had seen so many times under Eddie Howe when up against Mikel Arteta. Only Matthias Jaissle having to do it with an admittedly lower quality team, no disrespect and all that.

However, those in black and white elevated themselves as a team, they were greater than the sum of their parts.

Whatever Matthias Jaissle had said to them at the break, when added to the changes made, it was stunning.

Arsenal were clearly not expecting this in any way, United players flooding forward in such a brave high press. Joe Willock forced Martin Odegaard into losing possession, William Osula swept forward with the loose ball and a perfect pass for Harvey Barnes to do what Harvey Barnes does.

An equaliser four minutes into the second half, so sit back and defend a 1-1?

Matthias Jaissle ordering his team to get at Arsenal, drive them back, force errors, potentially more chances…

Just after the hour mark it is Tino Livramento of all people who forces a defender, then David Raya in his six yard box into mistakes that resulted in a corner.

A brilliant corner kick routine sees Arsenal out-Arsenaled, defenders blocked off and Dan Burn totally unmarked, his header parried but Joe Willock doing brilliantly to nudge the ball away from defenders despite pinned by opponents on the ground, on the line, Malick Thiaw smashing the ball home from a few inches out. Wow.

Sit back and try to defend a 2-1 for the next 37 minutes?

Matthias Jaissle insisting that his rejuvenated team keep taking the game to Arsenal.

Those remaining 37 minutes saw Newcastle United created more and better chances.

Arsenal scored a goal on the break which was brilliantly worked but still needed to go through a defender’s legs and a shot that Hornicek should probably have saved. That’s football.

Newcastle United didn’t take any of their chances and so it ended 2-2.

What a match and what an astonishing second half.

This was so so good from Matthias Jaissle.

The coward’s way would have been to approach the second half with a mentality of keeping it tight and running the clock down. Arsenal would have kept the ball for 90% of the time, happy to take a 1-0 or 2-0 win back to London, Newcastle would have been the victims of a predictable loss.

The minority of boo boys were vocal once again at half-time with United trailing to the champions/champions-elect.

By going for it after the break, Matthias Jaissle would have known Arsenal the massive favourites to get a second goal as gaps appeared and it could easily end a very messy three or four goal home defeat.

Yet he didn’t take the coward’s way, Matthias Jaissle went for it and Newcastle United (and their fans) got the reward.

He is for sure still learning the Premier League ropes but I think he has something about him.

Certainly enough to suggest that he deserves a proper fair chance.

The uber Matthias Jaissle critics say Newcastle United desperately need a Premier League proven manager. Rarely, if ever, do they ever name this mythical creature.

What exactly do they mean by Premier League proven? We aren’t getting Pep Guardiola or Jurgen Klopp!

What we would be getting is Premier League proven failures.

Yes, let’s get Sean Dyche in. I can’t wait.

Yes, let’s get Rafa Benitez back and ruin all those great memories we have of how he stood by us at our moment of need. Rafa’s career has fallen off a cliff since NUFC and it would be horrific to see him come back and get abuse when he failed.

All managers have to start somewhere, only a very small handful of individuals who were stellar players then get gifted a top club in their first job as manager.

Matthias Jaissle has done well in Austria and Saudi Arabia.

Now he deserves a fair and proper chance in the Premier League, with Newcastle United.

#1965. Italy U21 coach discusses Cisse’s rise, next steps for Camarda and why Bartesaghi is ‘a luxury’

Italy’s U21 head coach, Silvio Baldini, has shared his thoughts on the Milan trio Alphadjo Cisse, Francesco Camarda and Davide Bartesaghi.

In recent years, Milan have shifted more towards giving some of their academy graduates more playing time with the first team. Bartesaghi was the first to properly get in, cementing his spot in the starting eleven last season, while Cisse has been the big breakthrough this season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Camarda has had a tougher time after a loan spell at Lecce, but Milan have made it very clear through renewals and words that they will focus more on the youngsters. It’s exciting times as well, given how they have all performed with the U21 national team too.

Speaking to Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Italy’s U21 coach Silvio Baldini was asked about the breakthrough of Cisse, Camarda’s current state of mind and why Bartesaghi is a ‘luxury’ for his team. Safe to say that he likes the trio a lot.

Cisse has had a proper breakthrough. Did you see that coming?

“Compared to a year ago, I can see a different guy, who’s more mature and prepared, with higher self-esteem, psychologically changed, simply stronger.

“He has Milan to thank for signing him from Catanzaro in Serie B, believing in him and making room for him, then giving him consistent playing time. If he then makes the national team and does well, so much the better.”

Milan deserve credit, and you also deserve credit for discovering him as a centre-forward…

“Analysing training sessions, a series of situations emerged where he managed to score by attacking space and depth: if you can do it on the right and left, it means you can also do it in the centre. But even there, the credit goes entirely to the staff.

“They had the intuition, realising that Cisse could be useful to our game system in that way and at the same time, allowing Alpha to discover a new role successfully. I’m simply honest and meritocratic in my choices.

“Even though the goal against Armenia actually came from him as a second striker, at the end of that match we had two centre-forwards, him and Camarda.”

Camarda, by the way, has struggled at Milan but scored for the U21s. How is that possible?

“I can only speak about the work we do together. I spoke to him at length, I dedicated time to him, I asked him to explain his concerns, his fear of not being able to express himself as he would like. I told him stories of my own life, of how I came out of it.

“A dialogue not as a coach-player but as a son, or rather a grandson, as he could be, and a grandfather: from the heart. I’m not interested in performances as an end in themselves; they will come if he feels in the right place.

“I try to make him understand that I see him, I follow him in many small ways: he’s a conscientious boy who shouldn’t become obsessed with the goal, but rather experience football for what it is: fun.

“If, instead of fun, it becomes a test, then it worries you, and if you worry, you no longer enjoy it and it doesn’t help you perform at your best.”

To have more fun, do you recommend that he should leave Milan for another team?

“I’m not going to get involved in this. There are clubs, agents, and a family: they know what the best path will be for him. Let’s remember that he’s 18 years old, he plays for AC Milan and in the Under-21s.

“It’s clear that the more he plays, the better it will be for AC Milan and for everyone. We’re talking about a great player, a champion in my opinion, who needs to finish his development: he’s still growing, he already has a great eye for goal, and he’s sacrificing himself for the team.”

Camarda-Cisse: Can Milan provide the national team with one of the forward duos of the future?

“For me, yes. I see them as a permanent fixture in the national team, and of course they need to prove it and earn it on the pitch. But they have all the characteristics to do it. I found Alpha to be better prepared, even in his game decisions. Amorim did well to develop him.”

The third Rossoneri player is Bartesaghi: more of a full-back like with you or a winger like at Milan?

“Davide is one of the best players in his position I’ve coached in many years. He’s talented, very professional, mature, introverted yet open, and that’s not a contradiction: he has enormous potential, and he shows it every time he comes to us.

“If I were any Serie A coach, I’d take him with me. For the Under-21s, Bartesaghi is a luxury. He plays with heart, passion, and intelligence, as well as possessing high-level technical, physical, and running skills.

“He can play in any position on the flank. In my opinion, if he starts 50 meters from the goal, he can perform at his best.”

#1964. PSG rebuffed over Estevao and Rayan, eye 'much more accessible' Brazilian

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 12:02

Paris Saint-Germain have recently made enquiries about Estevao and Rayan, who are not available in the January transfer window. The capital club have a third, more accessible Brazilian talent on their radar.

Injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue could force PSG to revise their plans for the January window. Both forwards have suffered anterior cruciate ligament ruptures and could miss the whole season. Faced with these two major absences, boss Luis Enrique and Luis Campos are studying different options to strengthen the Parisian attack.

With Eli Junior Kroupi and Paris Brunner ruled out as options, the French club have notably made enquiries about three young Brazilian talents in recent weeks, according to TeamTalk.

PSG contacted Chelsea to find out the conditions of a possible transfer for Estevao. The 19-year-old winger, who arrived from Palmeiras, is highly rated by the Parisian hierarchy. His limited playing time this season had raised hopes of an opening, but Chelsea quickly ruled out that possibility.

The London club are counting on their Brazil international for the coming years and do not wish to part with him, even temporarily.

The situation is similar for Rayan. The 20-year-old winger, who plays for Bournemouth, is also on the Parisian radar. But Bournemouth are no more inclined to let their gem leave in the middle of the season.

According to the outlet, another Brazilian gem is being closely watched by the Parisian recruiters: Alisson Santana.

The 21-year-old winger currently plays for Shakhtar Donetsk and is enjoying a convincing start to the season. The Brazilian has scored six goals and provided five assists in 16 games. His performances have attracted the attention of PSG scouts.

Alisson is regarded as 'a much more accessible target' by TeamTalk. Currently valued at £11m (€13m), the recently capped Brazil international would, however, be more of a long-term signing than one for the second half of the season. His profile could also raise questions, as he is mainly used as a right winger, while versatility is very important to Luis Enrique.

PSG have not, however, limited their search to the Brazilian market. Two other attacking profiles followed in the Bundesliga, Ibrahim Maza and Said El Mala, who has already reacted to the PSG rumour, are also among the players liked by the Parisian recruitment team.

The recruitment team still have six weeks before the January transfer window opens.

#1963. Former West Ham talisman finally gets his dream trophy after quitting east London

The manner in which some players depart West Ham along with the bad feeling that develops as they press for a departure on their own terms can sometimes be the lasting memory that tarnishes their whole stay in east London.

Such was certainly the case of Marco Arnautovic, for example, a successful forward who demanded a new deal, got everything he wanted, and then quit anyway.

However, with some players, despite the bitterness, the rancorous ending of their career fades in the memory over time, and their stay is regarded more fondly for the highlights rather than the bad blood generated at the close.

Not quite sure yet which category the career and departure of Lucas Paqueta will fit into as his stay at West Ham thankfully fades into the dim and distant past.

Infuriating, gifted, inconsistent, yes, but forever remembered for ‘that’ pass to Jarrod Bowen in June 2023, Paqueta’s ‘yellow cards for bets‘ two year saga became, sadly, the other defining memory of his three years as a Hammer.

Winning the conference League title was his career pinnacle – until last weekend when he finally achieved ‘the ambition of a lifetime‘  (huh) with his boyhood club Flamengo.

Looking on the bright side, West Ham fans don’t have to endure the ‘baggage’ that came with Lucas Paquetá

As reported by sportwitness.co.uk, West Ham’s former number ten referred merely to his time in England as ‘two very difficult years’ en route to winning the Brazilian league title:

““I went through two very difficult years in my life. I decided to come back because I wanted this feeling, I wanted to feel welcomed, to be at the club I love.”

“I have no words to describe what I’m feeling. I arrived at this club when I was eight years old. My biggest dream was always to win trophies wearing this shirt.”

Well done, Lucas. We’re all very happy for you.

It feels a bit like learning an ‘ex’ has got remarried. Good for them. So what? I’m so over them now…

#1961. Premier League KMI Panel unanimously admits to another refereeing error which wronged Liverpool

The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has adjudged that Liverpool had a penalty wrongly given against them in a recent fixture.

The Reds won their last game before the international break, beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, although Alisson Becker was denied a clean sheet by a stoppage-time spot kick awarded to the home side and converted by Eddie Nketiah.

The penalty was awarded for what referee Tony Harrington deemed to be a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio when the two players unfortunately clashed heads, and Andoni Iraola said afterwards that he was ‘very upset‘ over that decision.

The Premier League’s KMI Panel has now published its findings from the most recent top-flight matchday (via premierleague.com), and all five independent assessors adjudged that the penalty award against Liverpool was incorrect.

However, there was also unanimous agreement that VAR was right not to intervene, as it was decreed that no ‘clear and obvious’ error had taken place.

The panel concluded: ‘The panel unanimously felt that the referee’s call of a penalty for a challenge by Kerkez on Osorio was incorrect, with the contact being inevitable given the jumping actions of both players.

‘However, the non-intervention of VAR was supported on the basis it was not a clear and obvious error.’

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Liverpool fans must be getting sick of hearing from the Premier League’s KMI Panel at this stage, with this incident coming fresh off the back of the panel ruling that we should’ve had a penalty for Jurrien Timber’s blatant shirt pull on Alexander Isak in the 0-1 defeat to Arsenal.

The incident with Kerkez and Osorio wasn’t as black-and-white, but the decision to award a spot kick still felt rather curious at the time. Luckily for Harrington, it came too late to have any major bearing on the overall result at Selhurst Park.

Still, to hear that an independent panel unanimously acknowledged that the Reds were wronged by another refereeing error is galling for everyone associated with LFC, and yet again it calls into question the standads of officiating in the Premier League.

It’s the kind of inconsistency between Kerkez having a spot kick given against him for a 50/50 duel, and Timber getting away with a blatant infringement, which drives players, coaches, fans and pundits absolutely berserk.

Thankfully the decision in the Palace game didn’t do any lasting harm for Liverpool, but you get the sense that it won’t be long before another contentious decision goes against us and the KPI Panel is wheeled out to tell us what we can already deduce for ourselves.
